### [21] [Label-Efficient Document-Grounded Factuality Detection via Cross-Paraphrastic Invariance Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16264)
*Chao Chen,Shanshan Lin,Dongsheng Hong,Sibo Ju,Wenjie Yang,Sihong Xie,Xiangwen Liao*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: CPIL（Cross-Paraphrastic Invariance Learning）是一种两阶段孪生网络（Siameseness）框架，用「跨释义正样本对 + 同文档异标签负样本对 + 分位数感知的半难负例挖掘」把少量事实性标注转化为关系式监督，无需额外人工/LLM 标注；推理阶段只做一次编码器-分类器前向，无需生成释义、成对比较或挖掘。在 11 任务 LLM-AggreFact 基准上，仅用 FactCG 标注池 2%/3% 即取得宏平均 F1 分别为 81.04 / 81.60，优于所比较的全部紧凑型检测器（CCHD 79.73、FactCG 77.14 等）以及三个 vanilla LLM 参考中的两个。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 文档基础事实性检测（document-grounded factuality detection）面临「监督成本 vs 推理成本」的两难：LLM-as-evaluator（SelfCheckGPT、G-Eval、SAFE 等）虽灵活但需重复提示、长上下文推理、多步验证或多轮采样，推理开销高；紧凑型检测器（AlignScore、MiniCheck、FactCG）部署高效，却依赖大量人工标注或 LLM/图结构合成的训练语料。核心问题是：如何仅用极少量（2%–3%）的事实性标签，仍训练出既准确又推理高效的检测器。作者指出，标准的实例级分类每个标注样本只能提供 1 个监督信号，而同一标签实际上可以诱导出跨视图的成对结构化约束；且通用的对比学习配对（SimCLR、SupCon、孪生网络）与「文档-声明支撑关系」这一任务本身对齐不佳——跨文档负例可被主题/领域/长度/写作风格等捷径区分，同标签但证据无关的样本又构不成有效正例。此外，负例难度需动态控制：均匀采样的同文档负例会随训练变易，而最相似的异标签对又可能因释义漂移、标注歧义或证据不足而过于「正样化」。

Method: 1）问题形式化：D={(d_i,c_i,y_i)}，y∈{0,1} 表示声明是否被文档支撑，检测器 h(d,c)=Pr(y=1|d,c)；仅复用已标注子集 D_s，不新增事实性标签。2）标签保持的释义视图：对每个样本用回译（back-translation，pivot 语言 P={fr,es,zh}，Google Translate API）生成最多 3 个视图，与原视图组成 V={0}∪P；基于「标签保持条件」——若释义同时保持文档与声明的事实内容，其支撑关系应不变，故各视图继承原标签 y_i。3）正样本对 D⁺：同一 document-claim 实例的不同视图两两配对（p<q 避免重复），强制不同表面形式在表示空间中接近，learn 释义不变性而非仅做 append 式数据增广。4）负样本对 D⁻：同一源文档下、标签相反的两个声明（约束在原始视图上判定，因为释义会改变措辞），从而固定证据来源、消除主题捷径；两侧均可用释义视图。5）分位数感知的半难负例挖掘（每 epoch 动态刷新）：均匀采样 K 个正对 → 用当前编码器 f_{θ,t}（无梯度）计算余弦相似度 s_t；取正对相似度的第 ρ 分位数（ρ=10%）作为安全边界 τ_t，剔除 s_t>τ_t 的「过于正样化」候选得到 M_t^safe；有效预算 K_t=min{K,|M_t^safe|}；其中 Top_{⌊λK_t⌋} 为利用型半难负例（λ=0.8），其余从安全池均匀采样作覆盖型负例，构成 D_t⁻。6）两阶段训练：Stage 1 用权重共享双塔 + 成对排序损失 L_ctr = mean max{0, s(r⁻)−s(r⁺)+α}（margin α=1.5）预训练编码器（DeBERTa-v3-large，最大长度 2046 token）；Stage 2 固定 Stage-1 权重初始化，接线性头 g_φ，用 BCE 在同一低预算子集上联合微调（AdamW，lr 1e-5，warmup 0.06，有效 batch 16，Stage 1 最多 3 epoch、Stage 2 1 epoch）。7）复杂度：离线构造成对索引 O(|D⁺|+|D⁻|)，每 epoch 打分/筛选 O(K+|D⁻|)（缓存共享视图嵌入可避免重复编码）；推理阶段无成对/挖掘开销，成本等同常规 encoder-classifier。8）评测：LLM-AggreFact 11 任务（dev/test 30,420/29,320），逐任务 F1 与宏平均；阈值在 dev 上按 supported 类 F1 最优选取（并列取更接近 0.5 者，再取较大值）后冻结用于 test，所有方法同一协议。

Result: 主结果（宏平均 F1）：CPIL-2% = 81.04，CPIL-3% = 81.60（3 种子均值，STD ±0.03~±1.85），高于 CCHD 79.73（+1.31/+1.87）、FactCG 77.14、MiniCheck 76.47、AlignScore 74.23、SummaC 系列 67.31/64.68，并超过 Qwen2.5-7B 78.20 与 Llama3.1-8B 79.29、Mistral-Nemo-12B 78.69 中的多数；任务层面 CPIL 在 Expert、LFQA、RAG、MediaS 等任务上优势明显，但 WiCE/REVEAL/Claim/Truth 等任务相对 CCHD 略低（如 2% 时 WiCE 56.39 vs 70.70，RAGTruth 82.40 vs 87.40），呈互补性。消融（2% 预算）：去掉 Stage 1 降至 76.81（−4.23）；Append-Only 增广 77.34（−3.70）；Random All Pairs 77.44（−3.60）；Random Pos Pairs 78.77 且任务极不均衡（WiCE 47.02、RAGTruth 46.74）；Random Neg Pairs 76.15（−4.89，印证必须保留同文档证据约束）；w/o Dynamic Mining（静态负例）78.64（−2.40），说明收益来自任务感知的成对结构而非单纯的成对训练或更多增广样本。敏感性：标注比例 0.2%→5.0% 宏 F1 持续上升，低预算区间增益最大，3%→5% 变化已很小（0.2% 时即已可比若干紧凑基线）；半难比例 λ=0 明显最差，0.5–0.8 最佳，λ=1 略降，验证「利用+覆盖」混合的必要性。Pivot 语言：3 枢轴组合在 2%/3% 预算下均最优（81.04 / 81.60），单枢轴中西班牙语最强（77.95 / 80.42），法/中较弱（74.08/73.10、73.10/73.71），多枢轴优势在低预算下更明显（+3.09 vs +1.18）。

Conclusion: CPIL 证明在极低事实性标注预算下，标签可被「重写」为关系式监督：跨释义正对学习对表层改写的不变性，同文档异标签负对迫使模型聚焦证据-声明支撑差异而非主题/风格捷径，分位数感知的半难负例挖掘按表示空间演化自适应难度并保留覆盖度。其两阶段设计把昂贵的成对/挖掘/翻译全部限制在训练侧，推理仅一次前向，兼顾了标注效率与部署效率。相对会议版本（静态负例、较简公式与有限评测），期刊版新增动态挖掘、复杂度分析与更广的消融、标签预算/挖掘比例/pivot 语言/多种子分析。主要局限：回译视图的标签保持是假设性的（实体、数量、时间、否定被改动会翻转支撑关系，且未做人工筛查，仅靠相似度过滤兜底）；评测局限于英文聚合基准且依赖外部翻译服务；作者承认标签效率结论不涉及训练时间与总算力收益（存在一次性的回译成本）；未来方向为蕴含/实体感知的过滤、替代释义器、跨域与多语言评测。

Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent claims that are unsupported by a given source document, motivating accurate and efficient document-grounded factuality detection. Existing LLM-based evaluators often require repeated inference and incur high computational cost, whereas compact factuality detectors are efficient at inference time but commonly rely on large labeled or synthetically generated corpora. We propose CPIL (Cross-Paraphrastic Invariance Learning), a two-stage Siamese framework that converts a small labeled set into relational supervision without acquiring additional factuality labels. CPIL constructs positive pairs from distinct label-preserving paraphrastic views of the same document-claim instance and negative pairs from opposite-label examples associated with the same source document. It further introduces quantile-aware semi-hard negative mining, which derives a boundary from the positive-pair similarity distribution and balances informative negatives with broader coverage. In the two-stage training procedure, Stage 1 learns an encoder from these task-aware pairs, and Stage 2 jointly fine-tunes the encoder and a linear classification head for binary factuality prediction. At inference time, CPIL requires no paraphrase generation, pair construction, or Siamese comparison and uses only one encoder-classifier forward pass. On the 11-task LLM-AggreFact benchmark, CPIL-2% and CPIL-3% achieve macro-F1 scores of 81.04 and 81.60 while using only 2-3% of the FactCG-released labeled pool. Both settings outperform all compared compact detectors and two vanilla LLM references. Ablations and sensitivity analyses support the contributions of task-aware pair construction, dynamic negative mining, and multi-pivot paraphrasing.

### [22] [SMIC: Shared Multiscale Input-Reference Conditioning across Transformer Layers for Natural Language Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16270)
*Xin Zhang,Victor S. Sheng*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文提出 SMIC（共享多尺度输入—参考条件化）：从输入一次性构建一个多尺度卷积参考，在每层用各自的卷积变换该参考，并在注意力更新前注入条件化特征。其载体 TCT-SMIC（基于复数向量表示 CVTR + Token–Context Attention）在 ANLI 三个轮次上均取得参数量可比基线中最高的十种子平均准确率，且训练 FLOPs 低于多数基线；在稀疏词汇扰动下表现出更低的注意力重分配与更小的带符号准确率变化，并给出以平均 Jensen–Shannon 散度界定子集质量重分配的有限样本界。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: NLI 模型对局部词汇变化敏感（Glockner 2018；Naik 2018；HANS），而简单增大模型规模并不能在相同优化预算下带来成比例收益；ANLI 作为对抗性基准进一步加剧了这一问题。已有“跨层复用输入”的工作（如 shortcut-stacked 编码器、迭代精化编码器、looped Transformer 的输入注入、value residual learning、ExoFormer、FiLM）都只复用 token 级嵌入或前层隐藏状态，没有“先从输入构建一次多尺度特征、再由每层独立变换后条件化各层”的机制；而卷积多尺度模型（Multi-Scale Transformer、Lite Transformer）的卷积作用于下层输出，而非原始输入本身。同时，既有防御（数据/目标/输入/推理层面）与认证鲁棒方法都不属于架构层面的条件化设计。因此需要一个能在不单纯依赖更大模型的前提下，提升 ANLI 准确率并降低稀疏词汇扰动敏感性的架构方法。

Method: SMIC 分三步：(1) 共享多尺度输入参考——分别对 premise/hypothesis 的填充嵌入做长度保持的 ReLU 卷积，premise 核集 K_p={1,3,7,13,21,33}、hypothesis 核集 K_h={1,3,5,7,9,13}；含 κ=1 恒等初始化的 token 局部分支、两个高斯混合分支（可学习感受野比例 r=r_anchor+0.5·tanhθ，由运行平均长度 n̄ 与固定带宽 σ=5 确定中心 μ 并对核加权求和）、以及全局平均池化分支；四分支各自经 CVTR 映射为复数向量并以零初始化 softmax 融合权重加权求和，加正弦位置编码得到共享参考 Z^(0)=[R^p; R^h]。(2) 层特定条件化——每层对参考的实部/虚部各设独立多尺度卷积模块（同样四分支结构，逐层学习卷积核、感受野偏移、融合 logits），融合得 B̂_τ^(ℓ)，以零初始化标量 ξ_τ^(ℓ) 加到该层实/虚分量上。(3) 在条件化表示上执行 Token–Context Attention：Q、V 取自归一化实部、K 取自虚部，随后残差与前馈只更新实部，虚部直接传递；末层实部在假设最后有效位置分类。实验侧：FP32 确定性训练，ANLI-R1 上以 5 种子调学习率/丢弃后复用，10 种子报告均值与种子配对 95% CI；诊断包括固定长度 token-ID 替换下的注意力诊断（top-10% 删除/插入 AUC、限制在公共 token 集并重归一化后的条件 pooled-attention JSD）、表面文本词汇扰动下的带符号准确率变化 ΔAcc=BreakRate−RecoveryRate、Llama-3-style 真实值 SMIC 插件、预训练 ModernBERT-large 与 Llama-3.2-1B（取前三层）加/不加 SMIC 的插入删除诊断，以及消融（去 SMIC、token 级参考、可学习尺度 0/1/2/3、层局部参考、深度匹配、分词器检查）。理论侧给出命题 1（条件子集质量界）与证明（Pinsker 不等式 + Jensen 不等式）。

Result: 性能：TCT-SMIC 在 ANLI R1/R2/R3 的十种子均值分别为 39.03/44.89/43.17%，在 Table 1 全部参数量可比配置中均为最高，且训练 FLOPs 低于多数基线（如 R3 为 4.27k vs Llama-3 风格 5.11k、Pythia 9.77k；R1 1.06k 低于全部基线）。消融：去掉 SMIC 后 R2 降 1.17 点（CI [0.07,2.27]）、R3 降 1.39 点（CI [0.62,2.16]），但 R1 反而高 1.19 点（CI 含 0，说明 R1 上的低重分配并非来自更高准确率）；用 token 级参考替代多尺度参考使 R2 从 44.89% 降到 43.77%（差 1.12 点，CI [0.17,2.07]）；层局部参考（无共享参考）在 R1 仅 32.92%（对比 39.03%）；尺度数 2LW 最佳（1LW 42.47、3LW 41.57，R3），0LW 固定尺度虽 JSD 最低但收敛平均慢 1.7 epoch 且删除/插入得分最低。诊断：TCT-SMIC 兼具相对较高的 top-10% 删除/插入 AUC 与较低的条件 pooled-attention JSD，且带符号准确率变化均值最小；将 SMIC 作为真实值插件加入 Llama-3-style 可提高删除/插入得分并降低各替换族 ΔAcc 的中位数；预训练 ModernBERT 与 Llama 加 SMIC 后中位诊断得分上升（Llama 的四分位距更窄）。深度匹配的三层基线复现相同模式，换用 Phi-1.5 分词器后 R1 均值为 39.54%（vs 39.03%）。理论：任意模型均有 (1/N)Σ|p_i(S_i)−q_i(S_i)| ≤ min{1, √(2J̄)}（以 2 为底对数时为 √(2ln2·J̄)），适用于 top-10% 前缀，从而所有配置可在同一尺度上比较。

Conclusion: SMIC 提供了一种架构级方案：一次构建输入的多尺度参考、由每层独立变换并条件化，从而在从零训练的 ANLI 三轮上以更低训练算力取得参数量可比解码器/MLP 基线中的最高十种子平均准确率，并呈现较低的注意力重分配与更小的净准确率变化；多尺度参考相对 token 级参考带来可量化收益，跨层共享是必要条件。真实值插件与预训练骨干（ModernBERT、Llama）的结果说明该效应不限于复数 TCT 或从零训练。Jensen–Shannon 到子集质量重分配的界为跨架构比较提供了统一尺度。作者同时明确局限：规则生成的表面文本扰动未经人工重标注（尤其随机替换可能改变真实 NLI 关系，故 ΔAcc 只反映该协议下的经验敏感性）；Table 1 因基线架构与分词器不同而只比较整体配置，SMIC 的组件级证据来自同架构消融与插件实验；准确率比较限于针对各轮 ANLI 分类的从零训练，预训练实验仅覆盖两个骨干并只评估删除/插入 AUC；删除/插入 AUC 与条件 JSD 属描述性诊断，不构成因果解释或忠实性保证。

Abstract: Natural Language Inference models can be sensitive to localized lexical changes. We introduce Shared Multiscale Input-Reference Conditioning (SMIC), which constructs a single input-dependent multiscale reference and reuses it across Transformer layers. Each layer applies its own multiscale transformation to the shared reference and injects the resulting conditioning feature before the attention update. We instantiate SMIC in a token--context Transformer (TCT) and conduct from-scratch comparisons against decoder-based and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) baselines across all three ANLI rounds. TCT-SMIC attains the highest observed ten-seed mean accuracy on all three ANLI rounds. The ablations further support the contribution of SMIC. We evaluate a real-valued Llama-style plug-in and extend deletion/insertion diagnostics to pretrained ModernBERT encoder and Llama decoder models with and without SMIC. Across the evaluated perturbation protocols, TCT-SMIC exhibits comparatively low pooled-attention redistribution and smaller signed accuracy changes. We further establish a finite-sample bound on average subset-mass redistribution in terms of the mean Jensen--Shannon divergence between the restricted and renormalized attention distributions.

### [23] [Beyond Compressing Everything: Contrastive Memory Learning for Selective Context Compression](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16384)
*Sikui Zhang,Haowei Liu,Ziyun Gan,Chunfeng Yuan,Guangze Gao,Nian Liu,Boyu Cai,Bo Li,Xiaolei Lv,Jun Gao,Bing Li,Weiming Hu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: CoMem 是一个查询引导（query-guided）的选择性软上下文压缩框架：它用"对比压缩器学习"（memory-上下文对齐 + 同上下文硬负例挖掘）配合"双向流记忆"（记忆槽之间双向注意力、原序列保持因果掩码），让压缩器学会针对每个查询选择性保留证据，而非无差别压缩全部内容。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: LLM 长上下文推理昂贵且存在信息冗余、干扰项与注意力稀释问题，软上下文压缩（把长文档压成少量连续记忆槽）被视作高效推理的可行路径。但现有方法（ICAE、500x、PCC、SAC 等）多为查询无关压缩；即使是把查询与文档拼接的做法（PISCO、SeleCom、RAM），也未显式鼓励记忆槽按查询需求特化，实测中同一上下文在不同查询下产生的记忆槽高度相似（Figure 2），查询敏感推理被全部推给解码器。作者主张：有效的查询引导压缩需要比"拼接查询"更强的监督信号，需要显式让记忆表示在同一上下文的不同查询下保持可区分，同时仍保留上下文语义信息。此外，标准因果掩码迫使记忆槽形成无必要的从左到右顺序，限制了槽间信息流动与容量分配。

Method: 1) 任务形式化：编码器输入 [<ENC>, Q, C, <MEM_1..K>]，取末层 K 个记忆 token 的隐状态作为压缩记忆 M=f_φ(C,Q)∈R^{K×d}，解码器仅基于 Q 与 M 生成答案（K≪n），构成信息瓶颈。2) 对比压缩器学习（Contrastive Compressor Learning）：将记忆槽均值池化为 m_i，源上下文 token 隐状态均值池化为 c_i；以 m_i 为对比锚点、c_i 为 stop-gradient 正样本，批内其他 m_j 为负样本，损失 L_cl 用余弦相似度与温度 τ 定义，保证记忆既保上下文语义又彼此可分。3) 同上下文硬负例挖掘：每个 mini-batch 用同一文档配多个不同查询（每上下文≥8 个查询），使所有负例来自同一文档、仅查询不同，迫使模型编码查询特异的证据选择，而非依赖粗粒度文档差异。4) 双向流记忆：注意力掩码 A = [LowerTri(L), 0; 1, 1]，即原 query-context 前缀保持因果、记忆槽之间全双向可见，用 FlexAttention 实现。5) 总体目标 L = L_QA + λ·L_cl（λ=0.1）。6) 两阶段训练：Stage I 用 CLaRa 预训练语料构造约 160K 样本，联合 LoRA 训练压缩器与解码器；Stage II 冻结压缩器、在约 453K 条指令数据上仅训解码器。压缩比覆盖 4×–128×，文档切块 256 token。

Conclusion: 查询引导的选择性压缩需要比"把查询拼进去"更强的表示级监督。CoMem 通过对比压缩器学习（同上下文硬负例 + 记忆-上下文对齐）与记忆槽双向交互，使压缩记忆既保上下文语义又对查询敏感，在有限记忆预算下显著优于现有压缩方法，尤其在多跳推理与极端压缩比下表现突出，且支持离线预压缩复用。作者亦指出上下文压缩存在信息丢失风险，在高风险场景需配合人工监督，且压缩表示本身不提供额外隐私保证。

Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) advance toward increasingly long inputs, soft context compression offers a promising approach to efficient inference by converting long inputs into compact memory slots. Under limited memory budgets, effective context compression remains challenging because task-relevant evidence varies substantially across queries, ranging from localized evidence to multiple distant spans or information dispersed throughout the full document. Instead of compressing everything indiscriminately, we propose CoMem, a query-guided selective context compression framework that learns memory representations conditioned on both the document and the query. CoMem develops Contrastive Compressor Learning to achieve query-sensitive yet context-preserving memory representations. To inject a strong prior over query-dependent evidence distributions, we devise a same-context hard negative mining strategy by pairing a single document with multiple queries, requiring the compressor to selectively retain information according to each query's distinct evidence needs. To address the restricted information flow imposed by causal masking, we further enable bidirectional attention among memory slots. Experiments demonstrate that CoMem consistently outperforms existing context compression methods across compression ratios on question answering and RULER-NIAH benchmarks. Our code is available at this https URL .

<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>

Abstract: Laya is a small model that answers a multiple-choice question about a text in one pass: the question, the options (each with a name and a description) and the text form one sequence of at most 512 tokens, the window, in the English release. A longer text is silently cut at the end, and we measure what that costs. Test documents place a held-out row's text, the evidence, at a chosen token offset among distractor text; 177 items, five tasks, three checkpoints (released, short-row fine-tune, long-document fine-tune), four window sizes and 93,275 scored requests. When the evidence lies beyond the window, accuracy falls to 26.4% for the released checkpoint (27.2% for both fine-tunes), near the 27.0% of guessing and below the 35.6% of always giving the commonest label. Confidence gives no warning (AUROC 0.50 to 0.55 for telling cut from read requests; 0.5 = chance), and the runtime's truncation flag also fires on requests whose evidence was visible. The released checkpoint reads visible evidence badly once text precedes it: 38.5% pooled against 60% when the evidence comes first, so a larger window alone gains +6.2 points. Fine-tuning on long documents adds +27.6 points on visible evidence over the short-row fine-tune (95% interval +22.3 to +33.1) and nothing on cut evidence. That is an in-family result: training rows and test documents share generator and question types, and the main filler is of the training kind. With encyclopedic filler never seen in training the gain is +13.2 (+9.9 to +16.6), with rows of other tasks as filler -2.0. Among training-free rearrangements a 312-token window scan helps most (+11.9 points over the default for the released checkpoint) at six to eleven forward passes. Documents are synthetic, labels are LLM-made and one backbone is studied, so these diagnose this model, not long documents in general.

### [25] [MuSeToM: Multi-Sensory Evaluation of Belief Revision with Textual Cues Across Six Senses](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16662)
*Chunkit Chan,Kawai Chung,Sze Heng Douglas Kwok,Yuxuan Liu,Yauwai Yim,Tianshi Zheng,Haochen Shi,Qing Zong,Wong Kai Chung,Pak Hin Lau,Calvin Yang,Yifan Gao,Xiaoman Pan,Ginny Wong,Simon See,Yangqiu Song*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: MuSeToM 是一个经人工验证的纯文本基准（2,415 个实例，源自 BigToM 与 OpenToM），用于评测大语言模型在"心智理论（ToM）"推理中能否判断新获得的感知证据是否在认识论上足以支持他人修正既有信念，并推断修正后的信念状态，覆盖视觉、听觉、嗅觉、味觉、触觉、本体觉六种感官模态，含"干净"与"含干扰项"两种设置下的四个任务。对 18 个前沿 LLM 在直接提示与思维链提示下的系统评测揭示：模型善于察觉"信念可能改变"，却难以给出正确的更新后信念，且普遍存在过度修正偏置——把感知上显著但认识论上证据不足的线索误当作充分证据。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现有 LLM 心智理论（ToM）评测主要集中于静态信念归因与错误信念推理，忽视了一个关键社会推理维度：人在获得新的感知证据后，是否应当修正既有信念，以及修正为哪一信念。作者援引认知与概率/因果推断理论，区分两个概念：感知显著性（perceptual salience，刺激因突出而吸引注意）与认识论充分性（epistemic sufficiency，证据是否足以在不确定性下合理支持信念修正）。感知显著的线索（如附近牛奶纸盒上"杏仁奶"的醒目标签）未必是证据充分的线索；而人类会用感知证据推断他人何时应修正信念，因此稳健的 ToM 推理不能止于"追踪他人感知到了什么"，还需评估"感知到的证据是否值得据此修正信念"。

Method: 基准构建：从 BigToM（200 则结构化故事，含初始信念、致信念改变事件、非改变随机事件与更新后信念）抽取 100 则，OpenToM（7,000 条长叙事场景，含明确的角色间信念陈述）抽取 120 则作为源故事。用 GPT-4o、DeepSeek-R1、Qwen3-235B-A22B 三个不同模型族生成感知线索（每则故事为每个感官模态生成支持修正与不充分/无关两类候选线索），并生成多项选择选项（正确更新信念、貌似合理但错误的干扰信念、不确定选项）。三名人工标注者依据一致性、可得性、相关性与是否支持确定修正进行验证与过滤，形成三类线索：正例（Positive）、硬负例（Hard Negative，线索连贯、可被主角获知且与目标信念相关但不足以支持明确修正）、易负例（Easy Negative，与主角信念无关）。共 2,415 个实例（BigToM 1,169，OpenToM 1,246），正例 1,012、硬负例 477、易负例 926；六模态分布为视觉 750、听觉 586、嗅觉 309、味觉 153、触觉 445、本体觉 172。评测任务四种：Task 1 干净信念改变检测（二分类）、Task 2 干净更新信念识别（多选）、Task 3 含干扰线索的改变检测、Task 4 含干扰线索的更新信念识别。指标为准确率与宏 F1，并额外报告正例检出率 TPR、易负例拒绝率 TNR-e、硬负例拒绝率 TNR-h。实验覆盖 18 个前沿模型（GPT-3.5/4o/GPT-OSS-120B、Llama 系列、Mistral/Mixtral、Qwen3/QwQ/Qwen3.5、DeepSeek-R1/V3.1/V3.2、Kimi-K2-Thinking、MiniMax-M2.1/M2.5、Phi-3-Medium），采用零样本直接提示与"逐步思考"CoT 提示，temperature=0、随机打乱选项与线索顺序以缓解位置偏置；另设三名研究生组成的人类参考（与标注者独立），并做大量附录诊断：来源故事聚类 bootstrap 置信区间、故事级配对随机化检验（Holm 校正）、匹配上下文内的证据区分分析、硬负例上的信念状态四分类（保持原信念/采纳目标信念/主角不确定/其他）、提示措辞与三值选项的 2×2 实验、线索文本 TF-IDF 探针、仅线索输入的消融、以及自由生成/部分重构的污染检测。

Result: 1）所有模型均显著低于人类参考（干净改变检测 94.29%、干净更新信念识别 93.83%、含噪 90.76%/90.02%），36 项人机对比全部 Holm 校正 p<0.001。2）"检测到变化"与"给出正确更新信念"之间存在明显落差：GPT-OSS-120B 为 82.53% vs 61.04%，Llama-405B 为 77.27% vs 54.66%；最佳直接提示成绩为 MiniMax-M2.5（86.05% / 74.12%）、Kimi-K2-Thinking（75.40%）、GPT-OSS-120B 与 Qwen3.5-397B-A17B（分别为含噪 80.51%、77.84%）。3）系统性过度修正偏置：跨 36 个模型-提示条件宏平均，硬负例过度预测率 59.2%（95% CI 56.0–62.4），TPR−TNR-h 达 47.4 个百分点（43.6–51.2），TNR-e−TNR-h 达 24.5 个百分点；Phi-3-Medium、GPT-4o、GPT-OSS-120B 的 TPR/TNR-h 缺口分别为 74、69、61 个百分点。4）匹配上下文（138 组）内，P–硬负例联合正确率仅 26.7%（CoT 36.1%），远低于 P–易负例的 47.4%（CoT 58.4%），说明模型难以区分"充分证据"与"相关但不足的证据"。5）硬负例上 49.4% 的回答采纳目标信念、25.9% 归因主角不确定，说明部分错误并非简单的信念反转。6）CoT 对认识论相关性过滤的净收益平均仅 4.5 个百分点，且模型间差异大：Phi-3-Medium +23.9、GPT-4o +7.5，而 DeepSeek-R1 −12.2、DeepSeek-V3.2 −2.1，即 CoT 常以牺牲正例检出为代价。7）模态层面：视觉准确率最高（75.6%）但硬负例拒绝率最低（48.7%），味觉准确率较低而 TNR-h 最高（58.8%）；类别标准化后味觉反超视觉（77.48% vs 74.09%），说明部分模态差异源于实例构成而非能力。8）提示措辞与选项形式会影响过度修正幅度（中性措辞+三值选项下硬负例与易负例差距仍达 19.2 个百分点）。9）仅线索输入的消融显示性能大幅下降（MiniMax-M2.5 的 Task 1 由 86.05% 降至 55.93%），但线索文本 TF-IDF 探针仍达 67.8%，说明存在一定的线索伪相关。

Conclusion: MuSeToM 表明，当前 LLM 在"感知显著性"与"证据充分性"之间存在系统性混淆：它们能较可靠地察觉信念可能变化，却难以给出正确的更新后信念状态，并且在相关但认识论不足的线索上过度修正。含干扰项的评测与模态级诊断进一步表明，聚合准确率会掩盖"拒绝不足证据"能力的失败，因此需要把这两类诊断分开报告。论文呼吁在评估 ToM 信念修正时明确区分感知显著性与证据充分性，并提出更贴近真实、更具诊断性的评测协议。局限方面：感知线索由 LLM 生成，可能带有风格伪影（虽经多族生成与人工验证缓解但未能排除）；因源自 BigToM/OpenToM，污染无法完全排除（自由生成与部分重构检测中无匹配，故可能非主要问题）；模态比较受故事内容与构成混淆，不能解读为内在感官能力差异；人类参考仅为 3 名同质研究生的小样本，不反映人群水平差异。

Abstract: Theory of Mind (ToM), the ability to infer mental states in others, is pivotal for human social cognition. Existing evaluations of ToM in large language models (LLMs) mainly focus on static belief attribution and false-belief reasoning, leaving a critical aspect of social reasoning underexplored: can LLMs decide whether perceptual evidence is sufficient to justify another person's belief revision? To address this gap, we present MuSeToM, a human-validated, text-based benchmark for evaluating epistemic belief revision in ToM reasoning. MuSeToM contains 2,415 instances adapted from BigToM and OpenToM, with textual cues spanning six sensory categories, and tests whether models can determine when a protagonist should revise a belief and infer the resulting updated belief state. Using MuSeToM, we systematically evaluate state-of-the-art LLMs under direct and chain-of-thought prompting, revealing a pronounced dissonance: while models often detect that a belief may change, they struggle to identify the updated belief and frequently over-update on perceptually salient but epistemically insufficient cues.

</details>


### [26] [SPADE: Soft Prompts for Ai-text DEtection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16929)
*Alex Jiang,Didier Schwab,Chuyuan Li*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: SPADE（Soft Prompts for Ai-text DEtection）提出一种基于「类别专属软提示（soft prompt）+ 点互信息（PMI）+ 对数似然比检验（LLR）」的 AI 文本检测框架：在冻结的 LLM 骨干上学习两个软提示，分别逼近 AI 生成文本与人类文本的隐含「生成上下文」，通过对比式 hinge 损失放大类间间隔，推理时用两个 PMI 之差（等价于两个条件负对数似然之差）判定类别。实验在 EvoBench 与 RAID 两个完全 OOD 基准上取得 SOTA（AUC 最高 97.7/95.7，TPR@5%FPR 达 84%–92.9%），并显著优于零样本（Likelihood、Entropy、DNA-GPT、Fast-DetectGPT、Binoculars、NTS）与监督基线（RoBERTa、RAIDAR、DPIC、ImBD）；同时在跨生成器泛化、11 类对抗扰动、短文本、跨语言迁移上保持鲁棒，且推理仅需一次 batch=2 的前向计算（比再生成类方法快约 85 倍），仅存储两个 64 token 软提示。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: LLM 生成文本激增，AI 文本检测成为关键任务。现有检测器只看生成结果本身：监督方法仅从少量硬提示生成的标注文本学习，易捕获提示特定模式、跨域泛化差；零样本方法依赖文本似然/概率分布，忽略「生成过程」这一条件变量（prompt），在开放世界场景下鲁棒性受限。作者观察到：即使只用通用指令（如「使文本更正式」）对文本似然做条件化，得到的 PMI 也能比 NLL 更好地分离 AI 文本与人类文本（跨 Qwen/LLaMA/Falcon 成立），说明「生成上下文」本身携带超越似然的判别信息。由于测试时无法获知真实生成上下文，且人类文本并无显式提示，需要学习两个类别专属软提示来近似两类文本的潜在上下文。

Method: 形式化：将上下文 c（硬提示、软提示或隐含写作背景）与文本 x 在骨干模型 q 下定义 PMI(x,c)=log q(x|c)−log q(x)，即条件负对数似然 CNLL=C(x,c)=−log q(x|c) 与无条件下对数似然之差，衡量上下文对生成该文本的解释力。训练：对每个类别 y∈{ai, h} 学习一个软提示 c_y（长度 64，随机词表嵌入初始化），损失 L_y = C(x_y,c_y) + [m + C(x_y,c_y) − C(x_ȳ,c_y)]_+，即类内 CNLL 最小化 + 带间隔 m=1 的对比 hinge 项，防止软提示同时解释两类；两个软提示共享冻结骨干，可并行训练（单次前向批处理两个提示）。推理：对候选文本 x 计算 LLR(x)=PMI(x,c_ai)−PMI(x,c_h)=C(x,c_h)−C(x,c_ai)，与阈值 τ 比较进行二分判定（可跳过 NLL 计算，仅一次 batch=2 前向）。实验：在 MIRAGE-DIG（训练/验证）与 MIRAGE-SIG（按生成器家族划分）上训练，评测使用完全 OOD 的 EvoBench（5 域 6 家族）与 RAID（8 域 11 模型，仅取指令微调模型），指标为 AUC、TPR@5%FPR、macro-F1，模型选择用 pAUC@5%FPR；骨干为 Qwen3-8B-Base，并对比 LLaMA-3.1-8B、Falcon-7B。

Result: 1) 跨数据集：EvoBench 上 SPADE 平均 AUC 97.7、TPR 92.9%，RAID 上 AUC 95.7、TPR 84.0%，较监督基线高 4.8–25.1 / 8.2–26.4 AUC；ImBD 在 EvoBench 达 68.7 TPR 但 RAID 仅 22.8，SPADE 迁移性显著更好。2) 跨生成器（每家族仅 500 对文本训练）：AUC/TPR/F1 均最优（EvoBench 领先 4.9–28.8 AUC、21.5–67.1 TPR；RAID 领先 11.6–29.4 AUC）。3) 消融：去掉 hinge 项（改交叉熵）LLR 的 AUC/TPR 下降 2.0–16.0 / 7.7–37.4；LLR 优于单一软提示评分（EvoBench +7.0 AUC、+11.4 TPR）。4) 骨干鲁棒性：性能主要取决于骨干预训练质量而非规模；Falcon-7B 上 RAID 略逊于 Binoculars/NTS（-0.6 TPR）。5) 对抗扰动：11 种攻击平均 AUC 95.6 vs ImBD 93.1（p=0.005）、TPR 84.4 vs 70.3（p=0.008），但对释义（paraphrase）与零宽字符（zero-width space）攻击仍脆弱（LLaMA 上 92.1→22.7 TPR）。6) 短文本：75 token 时仍达 98.2 AUC（ImBD 88.6，Binoculars/Fast-DetectGPT 78.7）。7) 效率：0.141 s/doc，比 DNA-GPT/DPIC/RAIDAR 快约 77–96 倍，比 Binoculars 快。8) 跨语言（DetectRL-X）：高复杂度语言 F1 约 95.0，印欧→闪米特/汉藏语系迁移几乎无损失（95.68→95.54），但英语→德语降至 64.45。9) 局限：对 base 模型生成文本明显下降（Cohere −11.4、Mistral −21.3、MPT −18.0 AUC），可能源于训练仅用指令微调模型、base 模型受指令影响弱。

Conclusion: SPADE 证明「建模生成上下文」是比「建模文本表面/似然分布」更可迁移的检测范式：通过类别专属软提示 + PMI 的对数似然比检验，在跨数据集、跨生成器、低假阳率、扰动与短文本场景下均优于零样本与监督基线，同时保持参数高效（仅两个软提示、骨干冻结）与推理高效。作者计划将该框架扩展到模型溯源（model attribution）任务，并利用 LLR 的逐 token 可分解性分析其捕获的判别特征；未来工作包括在含扰动文本的数据上训练以对抗释义攻击、以及面向 base 模型的改进。

Abstract: The easy access to Large Language Models (LLMs) has made AI-generated texts on the web increasingly ubiquitous, making AI-text detection a crucial task. Prompts greatly influence the generation process, but existing detectors focus solely on the generated texts --- supervised methods learn from labeled texts only, and zero-shot methods rely on the text's probability distributions --- ignoring the underlying generation process, which limits their robustness in open-world scenarios. We introduce SPADE: Soft Prompts for Ai-text DEtection, a novel framework for detecting AI-generated text that transfers better across datasets. Specifically, we measure the prompt's influence and use it as a discriminative signal. We characterize the prompt's influence by introducing a Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) term that captures how much a prompt explains a text. Based on this quantity, SPADE trains one soft prompt per class to amplify the separation, and predicts the class whose prompt best explains the candidate text. Extensive experiments on several benchmarks against various detectors demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of our method, achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on out-of-distribution (OOD) datasets.

</details>

TL;DR: Translated 团队发布 Lara Mini base：一个 7.2B 总参/0.6B 激活的 MoE 多语言基座模型，在 6T token（英语仅 41%，覆盖 44 种其他语言，含欧盟 24 种官方语言）上从零训练，并扩展至 128k 上下文。在 ≤2B 激活参数的开源基座模型中，其英语/多语言/数学/代码四域综合平均分（57.0）排名第一，领先次优 3.1 分；单用户单 A100 无量化生成速度比任何综合分更高的模型至少快 1.8 倍。消融显示把退火阶段的多语言数据换成英语仅使英语 +0.3 分而多语言 −2.7 分，且专家路由在各语言间高度共享，说明语言之间并未在小模型中争夺容量；作者主张"语言多样性是资源而非权衡"，并以 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 开源权重，另将发布 T-HellaSwag（110 个语言变体的 HellaSwag 机器翻译基准）。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 通用开源基座模型的预训练数据绝大多数是英语：作者审查的模型中非英语占比最高仅 12%（SmolLM3 为 12%、Llama 3 为 8%）。面向欧洲语言构建的模型给了多语言更高份额（21%–51%，如 Teuken-7B 51%、Apertus 40%、EuroLLM 37%），但同尺寸下分数远低于通用模型（EuroLLM-1.7B 27.6、Apertus-v1.1-1.5B 31.2 vs. Qwen3-1.7B 53.8），表面上看多语言数据"牺牲"了通用能力。学界既有结论（Conneau et al., 2020；Chang et al., 2024）认为在小模型中语言会争夺容量，但最新 scaling law（Longpre et al., 2026）表明该权衡取决于模型规模与数据分配方式。此外高质量英语文本有限，持续加大 token 预算会重复读同一批英语数据并收益递减（Muennighoff et al., 2025a），而多任务学习、神经机器翻译与表示学习均提示不同语言/任务之间存在正迁移，可提供互补视角从而学到更泛化的表示。作者据此提出核心问题：在小激活参数预算下，模型能否在不牺牲英语的前提下同时支持大量语言？并希望验证"语言多样性可能是通用智能的资源，而非必须付出的代价"这一假设。

Method: **数据**：从公开数据集（Nemotron-CC、FineWeb-Edu/2-HQ、FinePDFs、FineWiki、HPLT 3.0、CulturaX、The Stack v3、FineMath/MegaMath、Nemotron SFT 集等）自建 13.8T token 池；全池一次性精确去重 + 语言内/代码内 MinHash 近重复去重（去重后约保留 30T/50T）；用源语料自带的模型化质量分级筛选；用 Brown et al. (2020) 式 n-gram 扫描做基准去污染（前 3 阶段仅退火段执行跳过）；按"唯一 token 数的平方根 + EU 官方语言/优先语言加权"采样语言，把 EU 官方语言占比从 46% 提到 61% 的多语言 token；限制单源重复次数（仅 Wikipedia 及高质量多语言 web、高质量数学超过 1 遍），全训练 97% token 为首读。

**混合与课程**：四阶段——main 4.8T（恒定学习率，最宽混合）、transition 0.6T（混合向退火目标过渡一半）、anneal 0.6T（学习率 1−√t 衰减至 0）、长上下文阶段 100B（40B@32k + 60B@128k）。代码/数学/SFT 类数据占比从 19% 升至 40%；英语在文本域中从 44% 降到 27%，退火段多语言文本成为最大域（语言间 46%→55%）。

**架构**：decoder-only MoE，34 层，hidden 1024，Qwen3 分词器（151,669 词表，输入输出嵌入绑定）；每层 128 个路由专家（top-4，fp32 路由器，dropless，负载均衡损失系数 1e-3）+ 1 个共享专家，专家 hidden 512（细粒度，激活 1/32 路由参数），路由专家占 94% 参数；token 混合器按"GDN, sliding, GDN, global"×4 + "(sliding, GDN, sliding, GDN, global)"×6 排列，即 14 层 Gated DeltaNet、13 层 512 窗滑动注意力（RoPE）、7 层全局注意力（无位置编码），GQA 16/4 头、head dim 128、QK-norm；Gated DeltaNet 用门控 delta 规则与宽度 4 的因果深度卷积。

**优化与稳定性**：Muon（更新层内权重矩阵，含专家）+ AdamW（其余参数），共享单一学习率/权重衰减；峰值学习率 8e-4（由 1.2e-3 的小规模 sweep 外推后取几何均值）；batch 2048 序列（约 8.4M token）、序列长 4096、715,256 步；输出 z-loss 1e-4、router z-loss 1e-3；数据并行 + 专家并行度 4。

**评测**：自建统一 harness（lm-evaluation-harness 0.4.14.dev0，log-likelihood 走 HF 后端 fp32 log-softmax，生成式走 vLLM），26 个基准分英语/多语言/数学/代码四域，与 56 个开源 base 模型（仅 base，不与 instruct 比）按激活参数量分组比较；多语言基准只在模型"支持语言"上取平均；另评 RULER/ONERULER/HELMET 长上下文（对 base 模型改写协议）；推理速度用 vLLM 0.28.0 在单 A100 上以字符/秒衡量；并做三类消融：架构/形状/优化器（100B token）、混合注意力变体、以及退火段"多语言→英语"的 100B 双分支实验；另用 Belebele 同义文本做逐语言专家路由的 Jensen–Shannon 散度分析。

Result: **主结果**：在 36 个 ≤2B 激活参数模型中，Lara Mini base 四域综合平均 57.0 居首，领先 granite-4.0-h-tiny（53.9）3.1 分，且后两者分别训练了 22.5T/36T token（为其 4/6 倍）；多语言平均 56.7 居首（+3.4 于 Gemma-4-E2B），数学 59.9 居首（+4.7 于 Falcon-H1-1.5B-Deep），英语 66.4 居组内第二（低于 Trinity-Nano 68.4，高于 Qwen3-1.7B 63.8），代码 45.1 居组内第五。多语言 9 项基准中 7 项组内第一（XCOPA 与 Gemma-4-E2B 并列），INCLUDE 领先 5.3 分；即使用基准全部语言平均（非仅支持语言），仍以 49.4 居组内第一。44 种支持语言中 41 种优于同组最佳对手，仅简体中文、波斯尼亚语落后、韩语持平。它还超过激活参数为其 6–13 倍的模型（Ministral-3-3B 53.8、Gemma-4-E4B 55.4、Llama-3.1-8B 51.2、Apertus-v1.5-8B 55.8），并优于所有欧洲厂商模型。

**效率**：单用户单 A100 无量化约 1,100 字符/秒，与 ~1B 稠密模型相当；7 个更快模型综合分均 ≤42.6；任何综合分更高的模型生成至少慢 1.8 倍（最接近的 MiniCPM5-2B 高 0.5 分但多语言低 8.7 分）；多用户共享 GPU 时优势收窄。

**长上下文**：长上下文阶段后 RULER 32k/128k 为 76.6/63.7，ONERULER 32k 达 90.1（居首）、128k 80.9（第二，落后 Gemma-4-E2B 3.8），HELMET 63.0/54.7；短上下文几乎无损（Overall 变化 <0.1，各域 ≤0.8）。

**机制性证据**：退火段把 33% 多语言换成英语时，英语平均仅 +0.3，多语言平均 −2.7，9 项多语言基准中 8 项下降（最多 −4.6），数学/代码仅降 <0.5；专家路由分析显示首尾层各语言分化、中间层（第 10–17 层）几乎一致（JS 散度 ≤0.015 bit），且路由按语言而非文字系统聚类（塞尔维亚语像克罗地亚语、马耳他语像阿拉伯语）。

**消融**：0.5B 激活下细粒度 MoE 的 held-out loss 低于 2.4 倍激活参数的稠密模型（2.140 vs 2.285）；加共享专家与 Muon 后降至 2.098，AdamW 需 1.5–1.9 倍 token 才达到 Muon 同等 loss；混合注意力在 100B 消融中优于全全局注意力（loss −0.015，基准 +0.67 分），Gated DeltaNet 单独降 loss、滑动窗单独无效、二者互补，32k 序列显存仅为全全局注意力的 21.5%（128k 时 1.77 GiB vs 8.50 GiB）。训练全程稳定，负载均衡损失约 1.02–1.03；退火段 Overall +10.5 分、数学 +22.6 分。去污染检验显示无记忆化证据（MMLU 污染-干净差 −0.2，MBPP −9.2，均落在参照模型区间内）。

Conclusion: 作者主张在小模型中语言并不必然争夺容量：MoE 让不同语言共享专家而非分割专家，多语言数据对英语的边际代价极小（+0.3 vs −2.7），因此"语言多样性是资源而非权衡"。在此基础上他们提出更宽的假设——语言多样性可能通过提供对同一现实世界的互补描述而贡献于通用智能，这与多任务学习和表示学习的既有观点相呼应；但论文也明确承认尚未证明多语言训练直接提升通用推理或英语表现，且也无法区分收益来自 MoE 结构还是数据选择（消融仅覆盖退火段，未覆盖 main 阶段）。实践含义是：小激活预算的模型可以放心把 token 预算投向"见得最少"的非英语文本，并借助细粒度 MoE 与混合注意力（Gated DeltaNet + 滑窗 + 少量全局注意力）兼顾容量、速度与长上下文。产出方面以 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 开源 Lara Mini base 权重，数据管线与训练池未开放但混合比例在文中完整披露；并承诺发布 T-HellaSwag（105 种语言、110 个变体，含 25 种文字、46 个非拉丁文字变体；用 8 个无参考质量估计模型 + 分层抽样保证难度分布，两名 LLM 评审在 32 个共有语言上 98.6%/98.7% 偏好该翻译优于 Multilingual HellaSwag）。局限：仅为 base 模型，未做指令/安全对齐，不可直接当助手部署；各语言质量不均（阿塞拜疆语、孟加拉语最弱，爱尔兰语/马耳他语次之）；代码能力仅组内第五；HellaSwag 系公共数据，模型可能识别其英文原文对应的译文。后续工作包括指令后训练、扩大预算与语言数，以及在固定算力/数据质量下系统操纵语言多样性的受控实验。

Abstract: General-purpose language models are trained mostly on English: over open models we review, at most, non-English pretraining data makes up only a 12% share. Models built for European languages give them far more, but score well below general-purpose models of the same size. A common concern is that, in small models, languages compete for capacity. We present Lara Mini base, a model trained from scratch on 6T tokens in English and 44 other languages, which together cover all 24 official languages of the European Union. As training progresses, the 44 other languages together come to outweigh English. To give these languages enough capacity at low cost, Lara Mini base uses a mixture of experts architecture with 7.2B total and 0.6B active parameters. Among open base models with up to 2B active parameters, it achieves the highest average score across standard English, multilingual, math, and code benchmarks, ahead of models trained on 4 to 6 times as many tokens. Its margin is largest on multilingual benchmarks in the languages it supports and on math benchmarks. It supports contexts of up to 128k tokens. We find that our MoE architecture reduces capacity competition between languages. For a single user on one GPU, without quantization, it generates text at least 1.8 times faster than any model with a higher average score. We release the weights of Lara Mini base under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license. In addition, we will release T-HellaSwag, a higher-quality machine translation of the commonsense reasoning benchmark HellaSwag into 110 language variants.

</details>


### [28] [Auditing AI peer reviewers: a benchmark on real scientific papers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17052)
*Íñigo Zubeldia,Boris Bolliet,Francisco Villaescusa-Navarro,Pablo Villanueva-Domingo,Miles Cranmer*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: LLM-based peer review is now used at production scale, but its evaluation remains limited. We introduce a benchmark that injects objective, localisable errors of four types (general issues, mathematics, numerics, citations) at three severity levels into real papers and measures each reviewer's detection rate by error type and severity, together with its false-positive rate on clean copies. We also present Skepthical, a multi-agent reviewer that verifies citation-backed claims by retrieving the cited papers, mathematics with computer algebra, and numerical claims with executed code. We apply the benchmark to two corpora of 15 recent arXiv preprints each, one in astrophysics and one in machine learning (ML), injecting a total of 357 errors, and evaluate twelve reviewer systems: six single-LLM reviewers, two Claude Code configurations, three publicly available reviewers, and Skepthical. The choice of model has the largest impact on detection rate: given the same prompt, three frontier LLMs differ by about 50 percentage points in total detection on both corpora. Tools and scaffolding help when they contribute what the model cannot supply on its own. In particular, on astrophysics, Claude Code improves on a single Claude call in mathematics and numerics detection, and enforced citation retrieval gives Skepthical the highest citation error detection rate of all systems by a large margin. This citation lead, however, is not observed on ML, where the models appear to know the literature better and Skepthical's citation detection rate is statistically indistinguishable from that of the best single LLM. False-positive rates are below 10% for most systems, but vary with prompt, model, and scaffolding, with mathematics flags the main source of false positives. The evaluation pipeline, the injected errors, and the adjudication logs are released as a benchmark.

### [29] [Discovering Effective Agent Memory Designs through Program Evolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17068)
*Xinheng Ding,Seyyed Saeid Cheshmi,Ziyang Zhang,Tairan Chen,Wenya Xie,Yu Hou,Rui Zhang,Zirui Liu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Program evolution provides a promising approach to discover agent memory designs and study the choices underlying their effectiveness. We introduce MAPE, a framework that evolves whole memory programs from minimal seeds through a standardized lifecycle interface and an iterative diagnosis-proposal loop. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval yield an absolute accuracy gain of up to 12% over manually designed baselines at 35% of the serving cost, with further evaluations supporting transfer across serving backbones and benchmarks. Empirical analyses and ablations identify and validate two recurring design patterns: retaining raw conversations as retrievable evidence preserves details omitted from extracted memories, while composing retrieved evidence according to query intent helps the answering model use it effectively. Transplanting the composition module into five existing memory systems improves accuracy across all five. Beyond these patterns, the search objective shapes where computation goes: optimizing serving cost alongside accuracy shifts computation from LLM-based memory construction to selective processing at query time while retaining competitive accuracy. Together, these findings offer empirical lessons for agent memory design. Code is available at this https URL .

### [30] [Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation: Differentiable Length Control for Concise Clinical Reasoning in Smaller Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17128)
*Tanzeel Abbas,Ahmad Kamran Malik,Nafees Qamar,Sana Liaqat*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Smaller language models (SLMs) make it feasible to deploy clinical natural language processing where large proprietary models are too costly, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning allows them to be specialised on commodity hardware. One obstacle persists after training: on medical tasks these models answer at far greater length than the clinical question requires. In clinical decision support and point-of-care use, where time is short, such verbosity is hard to act on even when the underlying reasoning is sound. Existing length-control methods depend on preference optimisation, reward models, or proprietary teachers that undercut the accessibility making SLMs attractive. We introduce Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation (PECA), which adds a single differentiable conciseness term to the QLoRA supervised fine-tuning objective. Because the token count is discrete and non-differentiable, PECA instead raises the end-of-sequence probability once generation exceeds a token budget, a smooth signal optimised during ordinary training, with no preference data, no auxiliary model, and a single commodity GPU. On a 1.7-billion-parameter model fine-tuned on the medical-o1-reasoning-SFT corpus, PECA reduces mean response length by 72.8% while improving multiple-choice diagnostic accuracy from 40.8% to 44.0%. A sweep over the conciseness strength traces an interpretable accuracy-to-length frontier for balancing brevity and diagnostic completeness.

### [31] [Synthesis Smuggling: Maliciously Hiding Inferred Personal Attributes in LLM Outputs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17280)
*Gautam Galada,Supreeth Shastri,Sagnik Ray Choudhury*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: We propose Synthesis Smuggling, a novel threat model in which an adversarial LLM infers sensitive information about a user from routine assistance-seeking interactions and steganographically encodes that into innocuous-looking model-generated content. The user may then unknowingly transmit that information by sharing the generated artifact, say as an email, social-media post, or message, through ordinary communication channels. An adversary monitoring these channels can discover this information. We demonstrate this threat by training two open-weight models to infer gender and age-group labels from conversational cues and encode their predictions using invisible characters or word choices. These results show that user-shared model outputs can become a covert channel for personal inferences, even when the model itself has no direct means of contacting an adversary.

### [32] [Goal Encoding in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17297)
*Arnab Sen Sharma,Eric Todd,Sheridan Feucht,Andy Arditi,Rohit Gandikota,Natalie Shapira,Gabriele Sarti,Constanza Fierro,Lisa Schut,David Bau*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: We investigate whether and how LLMs encode goals: internal neural representations that precede and guide action, and that are flexible enough to be realized through many different execution paths. We construct a coding setting with multiple sub-tasks that allows us to evaluate goal-seeking behavior and the selection of sub-goals. In this setting, we localize an encoding of the next sub-goal in the outputs of a sparse set of attention heads. The same heads can be used to decode the LM's future actions in natural language (e.g., "I'm checking if a word is a palindrome"). We verify that this encoding is causal for next action and is plastic: transplanting it into a different environment, e.g., another programming language, triggers the same operation realized with a different sequence of tokens. The LM also sustains the encoding throughout the action's execution, which is puzzling because a transformer LM without recurrence cannot carry a state forward for more tokens than it has layers left. We propose that it does not need to. Under a non-recurrent goal-seeking (NRGS) account, the LM frequently re-reads the goal from the task specification, compares it with the progress visible in the growing context, and pursues what remains. We test the predictions of this account with targeted causal interventions.

### [33] [What Do Tokenizer Comparisons Measure? Disentangling Granularity, Root Assignment, and Word-Level Readout across Amharic and Hausa](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14818)
*Abdul Rehman Antall,Baidya Nath Saha*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Morphology-aware tokenizers are expected to help morphologically rich languages, and their reported gains over byte-pair encoding (BPE) are usually credited to their linguistic units. A comparison with BPE cannot support this attribution, since such a tokenizer also segments text more finely (granularity) and, on token-level tasks, changes how much the sub-token readout matters. We separate both factors from the effect of grouping words by their roots (root assignment) in Amharic, a Semitic language whose Ge'ez abugida hides consonantal roots inside syllabic glyphs, with Latin-script Hausa as an orthographic contrast. Our design combines a lossless root-and-pattern tokenizer with controls that change one factor at a time, in two independent implementations. In both, real root assignment improves Amharic named-entity recognition over scrambled roots (+4.9 and +4.7 F1), and root-frequency structure explains little of this gain. In small from-scratch models, the readout choice moves F1 by up to 13.4 points and reverses the sign of every comparison of the root-and-pattern arms with BPE, whereas in two pretrained encoders it moves F1 by less than one point. The granularity effect changes sign across languages and implementations. We recommend decomposing tokenizer effects, and reporting the readout, before a gain is attributed to linguistic structure.

### [34] [What Does Each Part of Speech Need? Contexts, Subspaces and Dimensions in Static Word Embeddings](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15114)
*Jintang Xue,Chengwei Wei,Yun-Cheng Wang,C.-C. Jay Kuo*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Static word embeddings give a word one vector, ignoring its different functions as noun, verb or adjective. Training on part-of-speech-tagged text gives each function its own vector, at the cost of a larger table. Using nine controlled corpora, we ask which context words each part of speech needs, whether it needs its own subspace, and whether the number of dimensions a word keeps should follow its part of speech or its frequency. The tags raise verb similarity on SimVerb-3500 at every dimension from 50 to 300 but help nouns much less. Added to verb-only text, adverbs help verbs more than as many random words; adjectives help nouns only slightly. At a fixed dimension, per-part-of-speech PCA bases preserve verb and adjective similarity better than a global basis or frequency-band bases. Nouns need more dimensions than verbs only among frequent words. We therefore allocate dimensions by frequency with these bases: at a third of the original size, only rare words lose dimensions, SimVerb-3500 and SimLex-999 nouns match the uncompressed table, and verb-to-noun retrieval stays within 0.02. Part of speech decides what a word's vector should be; frequency decides how much of it to keep.

### [35] [ShadowBench: Exposing Lexical Anchoring and the Illusion of Forgetting in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15925)
*Sujan Maharjan,Lu Liu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as primary interfaces for factual retrieval, yet current evaluation paradigms rely almost exclusively on explicit entity names. In this work, we demonstrate that LLM knowledge is fundamentally lexically anchored: models possess extensive factual information but find it significantly difficult to retrieve without explicit name tokens. To quantify this limitation, we introduce ShadowBench, a rigorously hardened, shortcut-resistant benchmark designed to evaluate Latent Entity Association via a novel Dual-Trait Association (DTA) task. Our evaluation reveals a pervasive "Shadow Gap" across all model scales$\unicode{x2013}$up to the frontier models GPT-5.4 and Claude-Sonnet-4.6$\unicode{x2013}$where removing lexical anchors causes performance drops of over 20%. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this lexical dependency exposes a critical vulnerability in AI safety. Applying ShadowBench to Machine Unlearning, we find that state-of-the-art algorithms (e.g., Gradient Difference, NPO) achieve only superficial lexical erasure. While unlearned models fail on direct queries, our novel Latent Entity Leakage Rate (LELR) metric reveals that for popular entities, models explicitly reconstruct the "forgotten" entity in their internal reasoning traces in over 74% of cases, utilizing residual shadow knowledge to solve associative tasks. Conversely, for niche entities, models retain high shadow accuracy (60-90%) via implicit attribute correlation despite 0% LELR. Ultimately, ShadowBench indicates that current unlearning paradigms create an "Illusion of Forgetting," demonstrating that existing methods act as superficial output filters and are not yet reliable for achieving true parametric erasure.

### [36] [Temporal Context-Aware Spam Detection Using Transformer-Based NLP Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16139)
*Fariz Zeynalov,Razim Mammadli*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Spam detection is usually treated as single-message classification, ignoring behavioral patterns that emerge across sequences of messages from the same sender. We study outbound SMS spam detection at the carrier level, where the goal is to predict at send time whether a carrier will flag a message as spam. Using a proprietary production database of 43,741 outbound SMS messages with UTC transmission timestamps and carrier delivery statuses, we report three sets of results. On an 8,749-message held-out test set, a TF-IDF + logistic regression baseline reaches AUC-ROC 0.8721, and a text-only DeBERTa-v3-base classifier reaches AUC-ROC 0.9011 and F1 0.8412. A deployed DistilBERT model augmented with inter-message temporal features reaches accuracy 0.8238, spam-class F1 0.8382, and recall 0.9128 at threshold 0.5 on a separate, class-balanced 20,000-message production evaluation set; these results are not directly comparable with the held-out test results. We also describe TemporalBertSpam, an architecture that encodes each sender's message history with a causal Transformer, and outline the same-split evaluation needed to measure its contribution.

### [37] [Pretraining Data Statistics Shape the Phases of Learning Entity Comparison in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16882)
*Yik Siu Chan,Jing Huang,Yanai Elazar,Atticus Geiger*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: How does data shape language model (LM) behavior throughout pretraining? We investigate this question through a case study on entity comparison, e.g., Between France and Brazil, which country is larger?, across nine comparison tasks spanning five entity types. We begin with controlled experiments in which we train small LMs (163M parameters) on mixtures of natural text from pretraining corpora and synthetic task data. Our analysis identifies three distinct phases of learning: (1) an early phase where the LM selects entities by frequency, (2) a middle phase where the LM selects entities by position in the prompt (first vs. last mentioned entity), and (3) a late phase where the LM selects the entity that is the correct answer. We show that the emergence of these three phases is causally determined by statistical properties of the training data. With small amounts of task-specific synthetic data, we observe only the first two phases and the model fails to learn the task; with large amounts, the model jumps directly from the frequency-based heuristic to solving the task correctly. Moreover, changing the entity frequency distribution from a naturally occurring Zipfian distribution (a small number of entities are very common and the vast majority are rare) to a uniform one weakens the frequency phase and speeds up learning of the task. Lastly, we show that the three phases of training dynamics from our controlled experiments appear in the open source model OLMo-2 32B. Together, our findings demonstrate that properties of pretraining data are causal drivers of heuristic learning and show that small-scale synthetic experiments can predict training dynamics at larger scales.

Together, our findings demonstrate that properties of pretraining data are causal drivers of heuristic learning and show that small-scale synthetic experiments can predict training dynamics at larger scales.

</details>


### [38] [Human or Synthetic? What a Fixed Budget Buys for Post-Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16895)
*Shourik Banerjee,Ethan Mendes,Mohit Raghavendra,Wei Xu,Alan Ritter*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Post-training of large language models typically combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with preference-based fine-tuning such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). Human-annotated and synthetically generated preference data differ substantially in per-sample cost, but prior work typically holds sample count fixed when comparing the two. In this work, we explicitly study the interplay between cost and performance by comparing the effect of post-training with human and synthetic preference data under a fixed, dollar-matched annotation budget. We train and evaluate multiple base model families across helpfulness and summarization tasks. We find that synthetic data is far more cost-efficient at low-to-moderate budgets, achieving high win rates with as little as \$200--\$400. On helpfulness, human data closes the gap only at budgets roughly two orders of magnitude larger; on summarization, it does not close the gap at any tested budget. We also find that human-annotated data varies in reliability: one widely used human preference source substantially underperforms another, and the gap persists even after standard remedies such as domain restriction and deduplication.

### [39] [Evaluating Pretrained Language Semantics for Structured EHR Prediction Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17053)
*Ashvin Gupta,Brendan Delaney,Alessandra Russo*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Structured Electronic Health Records (EHR) models typically treat each clinical concept as a dataset-specific token, discarding the natural-language semantics associated with the event. As a result, relationships between concepts must largely be learned from EHR co-occurrence, without directly exploiting any prior semantic knowledge. We investigate how pretrained causal language models can be adapted for longitudinal EHR prediction by developing tEHR. Here, we represent events with their natural language description and use this text stream to apply EHR-adaptive continued pretraining, followed by task-specific discriminative fine-tuning using LoRA, utilising the LLM as a longitudinal patient-encoder. We evaluate this approach across four prediction tasks on the MIMIC-IV dataset and pancreatic cancer prediction on the CPRD dataset at 1 to 12 month horizons, with tEHR using the Mistral-7B-v0.3 backbone achieving the strongest overall performance. Ablations show that performance declines when clinical descriptions are removed or misaligned, when numerical values are omitted, and when either stage of adaptation is removed, while explicit elapsed-time descriptions provide little additional benefit. Analysis of the learned patient representations further reveals clinically coherent structure associated with distinct patterns of disease risk and clinical history.

### [40] [Parsed, Plausible, Wrong: Output Format Controls Silent Errors in Small-Model Semantic Parsing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17169)
*Umar Ahmed,Maxim Dunaev,Mohammad Nour Al Awad,Sergey Ivanov,Ivan Khodnenko*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: A small fine-tuned parser that emits a well-formed but wrong tree fails silently: nothing downstream can tell. We ask whether the output format, a free design choice, controls how often this happens. On the PIZZA ordering benchmark we fine-tune two sub-billion models (Qwen3.5-0.8B and LFM2.5-350M) with LoRA on six lossless encodings of the same target tree, from 44.3 down to 10.9 tokens per order, including two matched-length pairs that vary surface form at fixed length. Across 300 runs (5 training pool sizes, 5 seeds) with a hierarchical bootstrap and Holm correction fixed before the results were read, shortening alone never helps, but writing the target in ordinary words does. The word encoding is the most accurate format on both models (87.5% vs. 85.8% exact match for the native s-expression on Qwen) while emitting 4.1x fewer tokens, and it cuts the silent error rate by 2.3x on Qwen and 1.8x on LFM2, separating at every pool size. Error analysis locates much of the gain in negation. All runs also learn to refuse off-menu input (held out: 95.9-99.0% handled) and to apply in-utterance self-corrections. Strict refusal has a measured price: 2.1-10.1% of real, mostly polite, orders are refused.

### [41] [ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17332)
*Jie Wang,Tong Zhu,JiaHao Kuang,Zhe Xu,Yunkai Chai,Dehong Zheng,Yu Cheng,Tao Ji,ZhouHan Lin,Qi Zhang,Bowen Zhou*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Model architecture shapes the scaling behavior, training efficiency, and inference cost of LLMs, making it a central focus of both industry and academia. In industry, teams such as those behind DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi routinely introduce architectural innovations, yet public reports rarely document which ideas succeeded, which were abandoned, and why. In academia, limited compute and inconsistent baselines often restrict evaluations to small-scale, single-point comparisons, making it difficult to establish whether improvements hold at larger scales or translate into broader impact. ArchSpace addresses both gaps as a public platform for Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing Architecture Researc}: each proposal is recorded with its experiments and reasoning, reviewed by the community, and referenced by later work. To evaluate ideas before costly large-scale training, ArchSpace leverages scaling laws to predict model loss at larger scales from smaller experiments, a practice widely adopted in industry. We provide initial references that make the platform usable: Qwen3.5 and OLMo3 baselines, fitted scaling laws, and a reusable training recipe. Ideas validated through this review can in turn become new baselines, and ArchSpace thereby aims to broaden the range of ideas that shape the next generation of models.

### [42] [Probe What-If Worlds Before You Ship: Persona Simulation for Real-World Decision Making](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14700)
*Julie Zhu,Jianheng Hou,Zhixu Silvia Tao,Shi Bo,Yilan Fan,Yixuan He,Zhiyuan Hu,Shirley Huang,Fangyu Liu,Yijun Wang,Zibu Wei,Haimingyue Xu,Zhen Xu,Zichen Yuan,Jierui Zuo,Jintao Huang,Yifan Wang,Qianfeng Wen,Jiahan Li,Zhejian Peng,Bowen Yang,Shushu Liang,Yuexing Hao,Xiaomin Li*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: User research and system testing reveal whether products and services meet user needs, yet recruiting specialized participants, designing controlled what-if comparisons, and repeating studies as designs evolve often bottleneck design iteration and data-driven decision-making. We present a framework and execution infrastructure that translates real-world industry inquiries into controlled experiments with simulated users. Our methodology formally defines the target cohort, experimental stimuli, and decision-relevant metrics, while the pipeline supports large-scale concurrent runs over cohort-stimulus-environment combinations (survey, web, chatbot, and OS app), auditable trial-level logging, cohort-level outcome aggregation, and cross-cohort and cross-variant statistical reports. Across twelve industry partner cases spanning five domains, we show how constructing hard-to-reach or what-if persona cohorts supports exploratory studies and distills simulated responses into testable design hypotheses. Cross-model comparisons on selected cases largely preserve primary conclusions, whereas perturbing or ablating persona attributes alters service outcomes, effect sizes, and inter-group differences, indicating that grounding target cohorts in detailed personas materially shapes simulation results. Together, these studies show that persona-enabled agents can test specified cohorts at design speed, diagnose systems under test, and deliver directional evidence that focuses problem definition, steers design and strategic decisions, and guides further study.

### [43] [An LLM Is All You Need: Data-Efficient Adaptation to Full-Duplex, Word-Level Spoken Dialogue](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14774)
*Tairan Chen,Richard Yucheng He,Yihang Liu,Baodong Cao,Chen Xu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Full-duplex spoken dialogue, in which a system listens while it speaks and can backchannel, yield the floor, and be interrupted, is usually obtained by training on hundreds of thousands to millions of hours of speech. This is costly, rewrites the language model that supplies the system's knowledge, and still leaves turn-taking either implicit or decided coarsely rather than word by word. We show that a frozen, general-purpose multimodal LLM can instead be adapted into a word-level full-duplex system with little data. Our system is a thinker-talker cascade on an 80 ms frame clock. The thinker keeps the LLM frozen and trains only lightweight adapters and a few new token embeddings (97M parameters); at every frame it emits one token of agent text, with pauses, yields, and onsets represented as tokens of the same vocabulary and kept legal by a finite-state machine. A four-stage curriculum, each stage anchored to the model's own behavior under the previous format, performs the conversion in about 30 GPU-hours. The talker reads only the thinker's discrete tokens, so the two halves are trained independently. On Full-Duplex-Bench and InteractionBench, the system is competitive with open-source full-duplex systems built through large-scale speech training: among them, it is the least likely to take the floor when the user merely pauses, backchannels most often, and leads in spoken-task accuracy, groundedness, and coherence over long conversations.

### [44] [Distributionally Robust BEST-RQ For Speech Representation Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14801)
*Muhammad Khan,Xiaodong Cui,Brian Kingsbury,George Saon*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: BEST-RQ, based on random projection and quantization, has been a well-established self-supervised learning approach to learn speech representations from large-scale unlabeled audio due to its high performance and efficiency. However, in BEST-RQ representations learned by random quantization can be sensitive to the choice of quantization targets. To address this issue, we propose a distributionally robust extension of BEST-RQ that seeks representations robust across multiple quantization configurations. Specifically, we define groups by codebooks and formulate the training as a group Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) problem. Rather than optimizing solely for the average loss across groups, our approach adaptively reweights groups to emphasize those performing poorly. Additionally, we regularize DRO with a Kullback-Leibler divergence to prevent excessive distribution deviation. We evaluate our approach on the Multilingual LibriSpeech dataset and show that the distributionally robust BEST-RQ achieves superior performance over the conventional uniform average across multiple codebooks.

### [45] [LLMs and the Homogenization of Teaching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14828)
*Mei Tan,Hyunji Nam,Hari Subramonyam,Dorottya Demszky*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models (LLMs) are known to lack diversity in open-ended text generation, a limitation that is especially consequential in education, where homogeneity can narrow the kinds of thinking and disciplinary work students are invited to do. We study diversity in two educational generation tasks: math items and essay feedback. We compare frontier and open-weight models with human-authored reference distributions using lexical, semantic, and domain-grounded measures. For math, we examine the mathematical activities students are asked to perform; for feedback, we examine the revision work requested and the rhetorical strategies used to communicate it. We evaluate direct prompting, two diversity prompting methods, and post-training. Across both tasks, directly prompted model outputs are markedly less diverse than human-authored content--78% higher on lexical (Self-BLEU) and 51% higher on semantic (embedding) similarity--and represent a narrower range of instructional forms. Diversity prompting and post-training increase variation largely through surface features without broadening the instructional repertoire. Models inherit and amplify the most normative routines of human instruction. Overcoming mode collapse in education will require richer instructional data and investment in teachers' creative capacity and professional judgment.

### [46] [Is Jev a Good Multilingual Judge?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14861)
*Wei Liu,Yi Fan,Xiyan Fu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Generative large language models are widely used for multilingual text evaluation, yet whether decision models that directly output judgment probabilities can serve as multilingual judges has received limited attention. We evaluate Jev against generative LLM judges on four multilingual benchmarks with human annotations, covering up to 47 language varieties and three evaluation formats: binary decisions, pairwise comparisons, and graded ratings. At approximately $1/31$ to $1/61$ of GPT-6.1's evaluation cost, Jev is competitive on most multilingual judging tasks, but falls behind GPT-6.1 on knowledge-intensive answer verification. Further analysis shows that Jev is more likely to accept incorrect answers in low-resource languages than in English and that its probability outputs help identify errors across tasks. Based on these findings, we offer recommendations on evaluation instructions, confidence-based selection, and model routing, providing empirical guidance for using Jev as a multilingual judge.

### [47] [Hy ASR 3.0 Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14908)
*Aoxiong Yin,Auden Li,Chao Huang,Chuanyang Hu,Eitan Wang,Ethan Zou,Fangming Feng,Guangyu Chen,Guinan Li,He Wang,Jiahong Li,Meng Yu,Mingyu Cui,Peng Wang,Rongjie Li,Steve Yves,Teddy Sun,Tian Zheng,Wei Liu,Yang Zhou,Yixuan Zhang,Zhennan Lin,Zhihang Xu,Zhuohao Li,Ziqiang Zhang,Anji Zhang,Bang Wang,Caisheng Ouyang,Chengqi Zhu,Chong Li,Conglian Xie,Dongdong Wang,Edward Wang,Evelynn Liu,Ferman Yang,Feng Lu,Gang Zhang,Jathon Zhang,Jaxl Liu,Jiachen Luo,Jian Li,Jingxi Gui,Kysun Wang,Liang Dong,Longsha Zhou,Na Hu,Qi Chen,Rilin Chen,Rui Yuan,Shanshan Sang,Siyu Yan,Steven Hong,Taihui Wang,Weiwei Li,Xiangyu Zhang,Xiaotong Yang,Xue Hu,Xue Jiang,Yameng Li,Yifu Sun,Yuhuan Zhou,Zhiang Chen,Zhibin Wang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: We present Hy ASR 3.0, a large language model (LLM)-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) system that delivers strong recognition accuracy, supports flexible contextual conditioning, and maintains robust recognition performance across diverse speech conditions. Hy ASR 3.0 supports Mandarin Chinese, English and 13 Chinese dialect groups, including Cantonese. Among the evaluated systems, it achieves the lowest aggregate error rates on public Mandarin Chinese, English, and Cantonese benchmarks and the lowest error rates on the corresponding internal test sets, alongside first-tier dialect recognition performance. Beyond audio-only transcription, Hy ASR 3.0 supports multiple forms of external context, including hotword lists, question--answer dialogues, and summaries, enabling the use of task-relevant information during recognition. The model also leverages intra-utterance context to disambiguate homophonic and phonetically similar keywords using information from other parts of the same utterance, without requiring a separate contextual input. Evaluations demonstrate strong contextual recognition in both external-context and intra-utterance settings, as well as robust recognition of long-form speech, children's and older adults' speech, low-volume speech, and speech in noisy environments. This report describes the model architecture and training methodology and presents evaluations across recognition accuracy, context utilization, and robustness.

### [48] [ToolTurns: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Multi-Turn Dialogue](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14925)
*Milad Gholami,Brendan King,Jeffrey Flanigan*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Tool-using language models are increasingly deployed in conversational settings, yet most large-scale tool-use benchmarks focus on isolated requests. We introduce ToolTurns, a benchmark of 2,620 problems spanning 1,827 tools and 11,004 API endpoints across 47 categories. Each dialogue begins with an intentionally underspecified request and continues through two context-dependent follow-ups, testing clarification, tool use, and retention of conversational context. We also introduce an open-source user simulator that reveals withheld context through dialogue and generates follow-up requests, with a checker--fixer pipeline for improving its turns. Across nine language models, the best agent resolves 69.6% of individual requests but completes only 39.8% of full dialogues. Under this evaluation protocol, every evaluated model receives lower success scores on follow-up requests than on the initial request, and dialogue-quality rubric scores and task success can rank models very differently. Paired turn-level evaluation shows that the checker--fixer reduces detected dialogue defects, and blind human evaluation favors the revised turns. ToolTurns provides a testbed for evaluating whether agents sustain task success across multi-turn dialogue with tools.

Paired turn-level evaluation shows that the checker--fixer reduces detected dialogue defects, and blind human evaluation favors the revised turns. ToolTurns provides a testbed for evaluating whether agents sustain task success across multi-turn dialogue with tools.

</details>


### [49] [CoLFA: Collaboration-Guided Lightweight Failure Attribution for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14980)
*Yufei Luo,Yuchen Ling,Chunrong Fang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Failure attribution in multi-agent systems requires tracing error formation to identify the decisive error step and the responsible agent. However, agents' division of work and information exchange lead to Interleaved Steps and Cluttered Content, requiring models to link executions and check details in lengthy records. This makes it difficult to balance localization accuracy and token cost. We find that multi-agent collaboration also leaves records of how executions connect and content passes between them as results are formed, providing evidence for tracing error formation. Based on this observation, we propose CoLFA (Collaboration-Guided Lightweight Failure Attribution), which uses collaboration cues to organize the attribution input according to how results are formed, determining which steps are examined and how their content is presented. Through Handoff-Guided Step Expansion and Cross-Referenced Content Organization, CoLFA helps the model focus on examining error formation and the role of each decision while reducing the processing of irrelevant and repeated records. Across five settings spanning Who&When and LongRCA and three backbone models, CoLFA achieves the highest exact step-localization accuracy with the lowest token consumption. Compared with individual baselines in each setting, CoLFA improves accuracy by up to 37.50% and reduces token consumption by up to 97.6%.

### [50] [FIBER: Bayesian Fusion of Fast-DetectGPT and IRT-Informed Detector Evidence for LLM-Generated Text Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15058)
*Yan Li,Guangsheng Bao,Zhipeng Chen,Guandong Zhang,Yanbin Zhao*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Detecting large language model (LLM)-generated text remains challenging under domain and generator shifts. Supervised detectors may generalize poorly, while zero-shot methods often rely on individual statistical signals without leveraging historical detector behavior. We propose FIBER (Fast-DetectGPT with IRT-informed Bayesian Evidence Recalibration), which integrates continuous Fast-DetectGPT scores with auxiliary detector outputs through Bayesian evidence fusion. Item response theory (IRT) models historical detector-correctness patterns, providing class-conditional detector-output likelihoods through marginalization over latent text representations. These likelihoods are combined with Fast-DetectGPT score densities and a historical class prior for prediction. When historical Fast-DetectGPT scores are unavailable, a variant called FIBER-Stream estimates class-specific score distributions from an unlabeled batch. On a 32,000-text multi-domain benchmark, FIBER achieves the highest accuracy (0.620) and improves mean AUC over Fast-DetectGPT (0.664 versus 0.600) under five-fold cross-validation. FIBER also consistently improves AUC across four individual domains. Under out-of-distribution transfer, FIBER-Stream achieved an AUC of 0.911, compared with 0.889 for FIBER and 0.922 for Fast-DetectGPT alone. These results demonstrate the potential of integrating complementary detector evidence and historical information to improve detection performance across heterogeneous settings.

### [51] [Where Language-Model Vocabulary Rose on Stack Exchange](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15172)
*Fengming Liu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Stack Overflow banned answers generated by ChatGPT five days after the model's release, and many other Stack Exchange sites announced similar rules. I measure the vocabulary of the answers posted afterwards, 3.8 million answers on 170 sites from 2019 to 2024. A fixed list of 56 words that language models overuse rose about 14 percent above its pre-2023 trend, while the highest of 1,000 frequency-matched lists of ordinary words rose about 7 percent. In a screen of 15 site traits measured before the release, the strongest predictor of where the rise happened was the share of answers that received a body edit within 30 days of posting. On the least edited third of sites the list rose about 29 percent relative to matched controls, and on the most edited third it did not change. The gradient is also present among answers that were never edited. It follows the share of answers edited by their own authors, and the share edited by others adds little once that share is held fixed. Use of the model is unobserved, so these results cannot separate lower use on sites with a high self-edit share from any effect of editing on what the vocabulary records. Any vocabulary-based estimate for the network as a whole therefore pools sites where the marker vocabulary rose sharply with sites where it did not change.

### [52] [A Closer Look at Language Model Introspection: Probing Information and Reporting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15267)
*Dustin Rubin,Vincenzo Timmel,Xufeng He,Aritra Saha,JooMan Kim,Vijay Madisetti*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: One way to study language-model introspection is to test whether models can identify where their activations have been perturbed. We train a simple linear classifier to identify the perturbed sentence from the model's activations, then compare its predictions with the model's own answers across pretraining and injection strengths. This tests whether the model is being asked to report information that is already easy to recover. If so, successful localization may be less demanding than it first appears and may not extend to the broader uses that motivate introspection research, such as faithfully explaining a model's reasoning or helping researchers assess the reliability of its answers. With an injection four times the typical activation norm at layer 0 and probe readout at layer 24 in OLMo~3 32B, the supervised probe reaches 98.3\% accuracy after 8.4 billion training tokens, while the model's zero-shot answer remains at chance (11.1\%). At the released base checkpoint, these accuracies reach 99.1\% and 89.6\%, respectively. Across 7B and 32B, location is already decodable in randomly initialized networks, showing that the architecture can support these traces without pretraining. In these experiments, location information lies close enough to the surface for a simple linear probe to recover it, so successful reporting need not imply broader access to the model's internal computation.

### [53] [Janus-MOPD: Tracing the Student Learning Dynamics in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15341)
*Zongji Yu,Ming Zhang,Dongcheng Zhang,Jiawei Zhou,Haotian Pang,Yiliu Sun,Xiang Wang,Youbang Sun,Chaochao Lu,Chen Gong*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Multi-domain capabilities are critical for practically applicable Large Reasoning Models (LRMs). Therefore, Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) has become a crucial part of the post-training process, integrating the capabilities of multiple domain-specific teacher models into a single student model. However, the student usually fails to acquire multi-domain capabilities simultaneously due to undesirable domain heterogeneity. Existing works have address this problem in view of temporal uneven efficiency and spatial hard allocation in external multi-teacher supervision. While in broader multi-domain training, varying degrees of performance degradation is still largely unexplained. In this paper, we shift the focus on how the student learns and integrates multi-domain capabilities internally, and then propose \textbf{\textsc{Janus-MOPD}}, a general learning dynamics framework of geometric representations for LRMs. Specifically, our main focus is on the internal performance of multi-domain capabilities on both temporal and spatial dimensions within the student. Temporally, our study shows that the student exhibits a Expansion-Consolidation-Optimization (ECO) three-phase learning dynamics, together with inherent limitations in learning efficiency and scaling. Spatially, we summarize two types of subspace locking within and across domains by tracing the representation space of the student, while explaining its clear learning directions but inherent cross-domain conflict. Therefore, \textsc{Janus-MOPD} yields a unified learning dynamics formulation, a geometric tracing methodology, and systematic findings of how the student learns and integrates multi-domain capabilities. Overall, we provide a \textsc{Janus} perspective to internally trace the continual evolution of the multi-domain capabilities within the model itself.

### [54] [Towards Better Legal Reasoning LLMs: Signal Balancing and Reward Scheduling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15346)
*Yinghao Hu,Qian Xiao,Yuting Huang,Kaisong Song,Yiquan Wu,Ang Li,Junjie Cao,Jun Lin,Kun Kuang,Fei Wu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: In the legal domain, LLMs can improve reliability and interpretability by generating explicit reasoning traces. However, training LLMs to produce high-quality reasoning traces remains challenging. Existing supervised fine-tuning methods struggle when reasoning traces are significantly longer than final answers, as the learning signal for the answer becomes diluted. Meanwhile, reinforcement learning methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization also have several limitations, including costly reward design, performance plateaus, and reward hacking. We therefore propose a two-stage training framework. In Stage I, JurisCoT-SFT employs a length-normalized dual objective to balance learning signals between reasoning traces and final answers. In Stage II, Lifecycle-Aware Backtrackable Policy Optimization dynamically evaluates and retires auxiliary reward signals based on their impact on final evaluation objectives, enabling efficient reward utilization. Our framework substantially improves legal reasoning performance on relevant tasks selected from multiple legal benchmarks, including ChJGBench, LawBench, and LegalBench. Experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements in both reasoning trace quality and final answer accuracy, while our models remain competitive with larger models.

### [55] [AraCrypto-ML: A Multi-Label Corpus of Communicative Functions in Arabic Facebook Cryptocurrency Discourse](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15408)
*Mabrouka Bessghaier,Mohamed Rashad Rouine,Md. Rafiul Biswas,Youssef Ayadi,Wajdi Zaghouani*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Arabic cryptocurrency discourse on social media is communicatively heterogeneous: a single post may report prices, explain protocols, promote investment, warn of scams, or invoke Islamic jurisprudence. Yet no annotated resource captures this functional diversity. We introduce AraCrypto-ML, a 10,000-post multi-label corpus of Arabic Facebook cryptocurrency discourse (2014-2024) from 2,898 public pages using a set of related keywords. Collected posts are annotated into six categories: Market Commentary, Educational, Promotional, Skeptical-Warning, Religious Framing, and Other/Unclear, using Fanar-2-27B under a prompt-only multi-label protocol. We validate 1,000 posts against adjudicated gold labels (macro kappa = 0.74) and apply Rogan-Gladen calibration to correct labelling bias. The two annotators agree with each other at macro kappa = 0.62 before adjudication, below the model's agreement with either of them (0.70 and 0.69). Reaction profiles differ strongly by function: Love is about 70% of reactions per post on Educational and Promotional posts but about 33% on Skeptical-Warning, which draws the largest Haha share (about 39%).

### [56] [Can We Make an LLM Dumber, or Is It Just Playing Dumb? An Empirical Study of Believable Performance Throttling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15568)
*Chengguang Gan,Yunhao Liang,Hanjun Wei,QingHao Zhang,Shiwen Ni*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: A benchmark score is commonly read as a proxy for model capability. We study the inverse problem: can a model be driven to a target score, and do its failures resemble those of a naturally weaker model? We operationalize believable performance reduction along three axes: target calibration, item-difficulty structure, and error-distribution similarity to a real weak reference. We introduce CapLadder, an IRT-calibrated suite of 1,985 items spanning mathematics, code, multiple-choice reasoning, and tool use. A simple weak-teacher LoRA dial reaches unseen target levels on reasoning with a 1.9-point held-out calibration error, whereas prompting, temperature, and weight noise cannot combine comparable range and precision. Yet on multiple choice, the dial converges to an answer-token attractor: up to 97% of its newly introduced errors land on one letter, with the attractor changing from D in Qwen to A in Llama. Logit interventions identify a dominant near-constant shift: subtracting the estimated shift on held-out items recovers 52 to 59% of lost accuracy and removes the dominant attractor, while option permutation confirms that the bias tracks token position rather than option content. With high inter-annotator agreement ($\kappa=0.94$), human-coded error-category distributions nonetheless match the weak reference on reasoning (JS = 0.00), showing that local plausibility and aggregate detectability differ. Structured tool calls exhibit more natural degradation in the Qwen family (JS = 0.09), while a globally calibrated dial transfers poorly across benchmarks (14.2-point error on two usable benchmarks). Precise score control, therefore, does not imply a portable or believable reduction in skill.

### [57] [VWEN: A Curated Small Language Model for Vietnamese Paraphrasing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15587)
*Sang Quang Nguyen*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: We present VWEN, a 0.8B-parameter model for Vietnamese paraphrasing at a requested level of change and for five related tasks: generating several paraphrases, simplification, gist, register transfer and paraphrase judgement. VWEN is Qwen3.5-0.8B fine-tuned on about 7k samples chosen by a four-stage pipeline: rules and deduplication, a bidirectional entailment filter, a divergence score that assigns low and high paraphrase levels, and selection for coverage and instruction-following difficulty. We compare it with paraphrase-only recipes from the same pipeline and with training on the ViSP corpus under matched and larger step budgets. On high-divergence paraphrasing, VWEN reaches a success rate (requested level reached and meaning preserved) of 0.61 against 0.46 for the ViSP model at matched compute, a difference that holds on inputs resembling ViSP. Given four times more training examples, the ViSP model closes the gap on such inputs but not on questions, which ViSP lacks and which it often turns into statements. Across all comparisons the entailment filter is the most effective stage. Training on paraphrases alone erases abilities of the base model that the multi-task data preserves.
