### [341] [Helgason-Fourier Random Features for Scalable Hyperbolic Latent Variables](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16461)
*Koshi Watanabe,Daichi Mochihashi,Hideitsu Hino,Takahiro Ogawa,Miki Haseyama*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Hyperbolic geometry is well suited to embedding hierarchical data, capturing tree-like structure faithfully even in the low dimensions where Euclidean dimensionality reduction is severely constrained. We introduce Random Helgason--Fourier Features (RHFF), an explicit finite-dimensional feature map for kernels on hyperbolic space. We characterize the spectral density from which RHFF frequencies are drawn, allowing kernels such as the Matérn family to be specified directly in the frequency domain. We also prove a uniform approximation error bound for RHFF. Building on this representation, we develop a hyperbolic latent variable model called RHFF-LVM, which requires no numerical quadrature, variational bounds or auxiliary variables unlike previous hyperbolic GP-LVMs. Our RHFF-LVM recovers the metric of a synthetic tree more faithfully than all baselines and attains the best mean rank, driven by large gains on tree-structured atlases at $Q\!=\!2$. Furthermore, it fits $5\times10^{5}$ points in $505$ seconds, making it the first non-parametric hyperbolic LVM to reach this scale.

### [342] [Learning Temporal Dynamics with Derivative Representations for Time Series Forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16514)
*Shujie Duan,Jia Hong Puah,Haocheng Wu,Yifei Mao,Hongting Zhou,Chenxuan Li,Zitao Fang,Yang Lu,Sim Kuan Goh*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Time series forecasting aims to predict the future evolution of complex systems by learning their underlying dynamics from past observations. Despite recent advances in deep learning, Transformers in particular still struggle to capture the temporal evolution of system dynamics. Existing approaches have been largely driven by architectural innovation, with comparatively little attention paid to training strategies that explicitly exploit the temporal structure governing system dynamics. In this work, we introduce DeltaTSF, a dynamics-aware forecasting framework based on discrete derivative representations of time series. Specifically, DeltaTSF jointly learns the series and their discrete temporal derivatives across both input and forecast horizons within a unified, model-agnostic framework. By coupling these representations over time, the model is encouraged to maintain temporal consistency, a property we show to induce a form of discrete Taylor consistency during training. This formulation enables the model to better reflect the underlying system dynamics, resulting in more stable and physically coherent forecasts. Notably, DeltaTSF does not require explicit derivative computation and introduces no additional computational overhead at inference time. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks and backbone architectures demonstrate that DeltaTSF consistently improves forecasting performance and yields more dynamically coherent predictions than strong SOTA methods. These results highlight the effectiveness of enforcing dynamic coherence through derivative representations as a model-agnostic paradigm that operates alongside and complements architectural design. Source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

### [343] [HALight: Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Control under Lane-Level Missing Observations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16574)
*Chenkai Hu,Yingqian Zhang,Ming Xie,Yi Fang,Chengxiang Jin,Chao Li*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Multi-agent reinforcement learning has shown great promise for traffic signal control. However, most existing methods rely on two key assumptions: (i) agents are assumed to be homogeneous with unified observation/action spaces; (ii) full and reliable lane-level traffic observations are available to all agents. In practice, urban road networks exhibit substantial structural heterogeneity (e.g., lane configurations and phase designs), while sensor failures and incomplete detector coverage often result in missing incoming lane measurements. Such issues can severely impair coordination and destabilize learning. To address these challenges, we propose HALight, a communication-enhanced heterogeneous multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for traffic signal control under lane-level missing observations. HALight supports intersection-specific observation and action modeling to accommodate heterogeneous intersections, and incorporates a lightweight one-hop neighborhood communication module to enrich spatial context when lane-level observations are partially unavailable. Moreover, HALight adopts a sequential policy update scheme to improve coordination among heterogeneous agents. Experimental results on two real-world road networks demonstrate that HALight outperforms representative homogeneous and heterogeneous baselines in terms of traffic efficiency and convergence behavior. The code and datasets used in this work are available at this https URL .

### [344] [DySR-GNN: Dynamic Sensor-Relationship Graph Neural Network for Root Cause Analysis in Automotive HiL Multivariate Time Series](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16623)
*Hamza Ouarrad,Mohammad Abboush,Andreas Rausch*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Root-cause analysis in automotive Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) systems is challenging because faults can propagate across multiple interacting signals, making the most abnormal sensor different from the actual fault origin. This work proposes DySR-GNN, a Dynamic Sensor-Relationship Graph Neural Network for supervised multi-label root-cause identification in multivariate HiL time series. The approach jointly extracts temporal patterns within individual sensor signals and structural relationships across sensors. Each sensor is processed by a shared temporal encoder and combined with a trainable sensor-identity representation, from which a sparse relationship graph is reconstructed independently for every input window. This window-specific structure provides an explicit representation of the sensor relationships used for graph message passing and direct root-location prediction. Under a recording-disjoint evaluation protocol, the proposed model outperforms CNN--LSTM, Static GCN, Static GAT, and context-based variants, achieving a recording-level Macro-F1 of 0.9524, MCC of 0.9302, and strict exact-match accuracy of 0.8519. Analysis of the learned graphs reveals both persistent and state-dependent relationships among sensor variables. The results demonstrate that extracting adaptive relational structure alongside temporal representations can improve multi-label root-cause identification in complex automotive cyber--physical systems.

### [345] [Asymmetric Multimodal Learning with Decomposed JEPAs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16639)
*Yusuf Shihata*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Cross-modal alignment is the standard objective for building multimodal representations. We show that alignment as a \emph{sole} objective is lossy wherever modalities are informationally asymmetric---where neither can express what the other carries. Visual question answering is an obvious case: a question is a selective relational operator probing a dense visual field whose fine-grained features no query recovers, so what alignment preserves is not what the task requires. We prove an \textbf{Alignment Redundancy Bound}: alignment-only Dirichlet energy minimization retains at most the redundant information atom $\Red(Z; X_1, X_2)$, annihilating private modality-specific structure $\Unq(Z; X_m)$ and cross-modal synergy $\Syn(Z; X_1, X_2)$. We introduce \textbf{Decomposed JEPA (D-JEPA)}, which factorizes latents into an aligned shared core and private modality-specific fibers. The shared core retains most of the structure alignment targets; the private fibers recover what alignment discards, via contextual masked prediction and asymmetric cross-subspace independence. Under information asymmetry, alignment-only training undergoes catastrophic semantic collapse on compositional reasoning benchmarks, surviving only on binary queries. D-JEPA averts this collapse, substantially improving downstream accuracy over both alignment-only and alignment-with-reconstruction baselines, and restoring a positive multimodal synergy gap in place of the baseline's inverted gap. Information-theoretic audits confirm that D-JEPA recovers most of the mutual information available from a frozen backbone, and causal fiber-swap interventions demonstrate that the recovered information is causally localized in the private fibers.

### [347] [Manifold Attracting Flow Matching: Physics-Constrained Sampling via Continuous Geometric Dynamics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16677)
*Guanyu Chen,Jinchen Wang,Shengze Xu,Xingyu Ren,Tieyong Zeng,Antonios Armaou,Dong Ni*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Generating scientific data under previously unseen equality constraints requires satisfying the prescribed constraints without destroying the physical structure learned from data. Existing inference-time approaches often enforce physical constraints by repeatedly correcting predicted endpoints, but such discrete corrections can distort learned generative structure and introduce unstable feedback. In this work, we propose Manifold Attracting Flow Matching (MAFM), which continuously evolves a persistent anchor through an ODE whose dynamics drive it analytically toward the constraint manifold. Specifically, its geometric correction preserves model-guided tangent motion while prescribing the normal motion to contract constraint violations toward the manifold. This construction separates model tracking from constraint attraction and provides theoretical guarantees for residual contraction and local feedback stabilization. Experiments across geometric and partial differential equation benchmarks demonstrate improved generation quality over variant constraint-guided baselines while maintaining low constraint residuals. MAFM provides a flexible framework for coordinating learned physical structure and explicit constraints through controllable sampling dynamics, without retraining the underlying generative model.

### [348] [On the Difficulty of Sequence-Level Supervised Learning for Autoregressive Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16736)
*Mathieu Blondel,Michaël E. Sander,Germain Vivier-Ardisson,Tianlin Liu,Vincent Roulet*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: During the supervised learning phase, autoregressive language models are typically trained by minimizing the negative log-likelihood of the training data, which decomposes as a sum of token-level cross-entropies via teacher forcing. This objective is simple and efficient but potentially suffers from so-called exposure bias: a mismatch between the way the model is trained and the way it is used at inference time. Can we instead design sequence-level loss functions that incorporate inference-time decoding procedures, such as greedy decoding or autoregressive sampling? We show that two natural attempts lead to loss functions that are fundamentally flawed: unbounded below. We further show that these two flawed loss functions are intimately connected: using autoregressive Gumbel tricks, the sampling based loss is the expected greedy loss under Gumbel perturbations. Since the pathology stems from the dependence of the decoded sequence on the model parameters, we analyze the update direction obtained by applying a stop gradient on the sampling procedure, leading to a moment matching direction. While it is not the gradient of any loss function, we prove that it defines a valid descent direction in function space for the autoregressive negative log-likelihood. Despite these theoretical insights, the moment matching direction suffers from high variance. We conclude that teacher forcing may well be ``all you need'' for supervised learning of autoregressive models.

Abstract: During the supervised learning phase, autoregressive language models are typically trained by minimizing the negative log-likelihood of the training data, which decomposes as a sum of token-level cross-entropies via teacher forcing. This objective is simple and efficient but potentially suffers from so-called exposure bias: a mismatch between the way the model is trained and the way it is used at inference time. Can we instead design sequence-level loss functions that incorporate inference-time decoding procedures, such as greedy decoding or autoregressive sampling? We show that two natural attempts lead to loss functions that are fundamentally flawed: unbounded below. We further show that these two flawed loss functions are intimately connected: using autoregressive Gumbel tricks, the sampling based loss is the expected greedy loss under Gumbel perturbations. Since the pathology stems from the dependence of the decoded sequence on the model parameters, we analyze the update direction obtained by applying a stop gradient on the sampling procedure, leading to a moment matching direction. While it is not the gradient of any loss function, we prove that it defines a valid descent direction in function space for the autoregressive negative log-likelihood. Despite these theoretical insights, the moment matching direction suffers from high variance. We conclude that teacher forcing may well be ``all you need'' for supervised learning of autoregressive models.

### [349] [Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16750)
*Nabanita Sarker,Hafiz Imtiaz*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Machine learning coupled with device simulation is widely used to optimize thin-film solar cells, but almost exclusively in the forward direction, from device parameters to predicted performance. The inverse problem encountered after fabrication, namely identifying the mechanism that limits a given device, is still addressed by manual inspection of characterization data. In this work, both directions are examined for lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells using approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations. Replacing the Spiro-OMeTAD hole transport layer with CuI increases the simulated power conversion efficiency from 19.6\% to 21.6\%, almost entirely through the fill factor. Surrogate models trained and tested on a factorial parameter grid substantially overstate their predictive accuracy. An XGBoost regressor attains $R^2 = 0.9997$ on held-out grid points but only 0.58 on independently sampled devices, whereas training on a Latin hypercube design of comparable size restores $R^2 = 0.995$. For the inverse problem, a multi-label classifier identifies which of six degradation mechanisms are present from simulated temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit-voltage measurements. It achieves a macro $F_1$ score of 0.938, compared to 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline. The classifier does not, however, generalize to combinations of mechanisms absent from the training set.

### [350] [Beyond Binary Classification: Multiclass Machine Learning for Diabetes and Prediabetes Risk Prediction Using NHANES](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16756)
*Aman Mujahid,Anita Penkova*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Detecting diabetes risk early is important for preventing disease progression. Most existing machine learning approaches focus on binary classification, which limits their ability to capture intermediate risk states such as prediabetes. We develop a supervised learning framework to classify adults as normal, prediabetic, or diabetic using National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data. The framework uses routinely collected demographic, clinical, and lifestyle variables from 15,356 adults, with glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) used only to define labels and excluded from input features to prevent leakage. We compare conventional machine learning and transformer-based models and examine two binary formulations: normal versus prediabetes, and normal versus combined prediabetes and diabetes. Models are evaluated on a held-out test set using precision, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. In the multiclass setting, performance is broadly consistent across models, with accuracy up to 0.72 and macro-averaged F1 of 0.70. Prediabetes remains the most challenging class, with F1 scores of 0.54 to 0.56 for conventional models and 0.53 to 0.55 for transformers, reflecting its overlap with both neighboring states. When the task is reduced to normal versus prediabetes, F1 scores rise modestly to 0.62 to 0.64. A more substantial improvement is observed under a broader screening formulation combining prediabetes and diabetes, with F1 scores of 0.73 to 0.74 across all models. These findings suggest that feature overlap along the biological continuum between normal and diabetic states contributes more to the difficulty of prediabetes detection than model architecture. Multiclass prediction provides a more clinically informative representation of metabolic risk progression but highlights a trade-off between clinically meaningful stratification and predictive accuracy.

### [351] [Class-Competence Aggregation: Output-Layer Routing for Federated Multiclass DDoS Detection under Class-Concentrated Non-IID Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16772)
*Tapu Datta,Hafiz Imtiaz*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Federated learning over distributed intrusion-detection sensors naturally produces \emph{class-concentrated} non-IID data, where an entire attack class is held by a single client and absent elsewhere. We show this collapses federated averaging in a specific, localized way: the output layer holds one decision boundary per class, and when a class's aggregation weight comes overwhelmingly from clients that have never seen it, its neuron receives an active anti-signal rather than mere dilution, collapsing to zero. On CIC-DDoS2019, standard FedAvg drives the concentrated LDAP class to $0.00 \pm 0.00\%$ F1 across every seed. We propose Class-Competence Aggregation (CCA), which aggregates the output layer per class using each client's own locally reported validation F1 as the weight, while hidden layers remain under standard size-weighted FedAvg. CCA requires no server-held auxiliary data and adds only one F1 scalar per class per round beyond the feature-scaling and class-count exchanges common to any federated pipeline. On our primary CNN-LSTM architecture, CCA alone raises LDAP F1 from $0\%$ to $84.83 \pm 1.65\%$, and the full method reaches $91.64 \pm 0.57\%$ macro F1, closing the federated-to-centralized gap from $-42.53$ to $-4.05$ points. Benchmarked against four other federated methods under identical partitions and seeds, CCA is the only one that recovers the concentrated class substantially and reliably; a $178\times$ smaller MLP shows the same qualitative recovery, though less completely, confirming the effect holds across architecture scale even as its magnitude varies. Results are validated across three seeds and replicated on a second dataset, CICIDS2017.

### [352] [ScrewSense: Mapping the Invisible - Anomaly Detection and Error Classification in Screwdriving Processes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16789)
*Tobias Lettner,Tatyana Ivanovska,Anwar Al Assadi,Christian Bergler*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: The growing volume of process data generated by screwdriving systems, combined with advancements in computing power, data storage, and algorithms, is facilitating the application of artificial intelligence in this field. Accurately detecting and classifying screwdriving errors is crucial for ensuring product quality, avoiding costly rework in manufacturing, and supporting sustainability by facilitating the maintenance, reuse, and recycling of screw-connected products. In this context, machine learning approaches offer a promising alternative to traditional monitoring techniques, such as window-based methods or envelope curves. This study examines the use of deep learning techniques for anomaly detection and error classification in screwdriving processes. The data corpus consists of multivariate time series capturing process parameters, such as torque and rotation angle. For anomaly detection, the embedding space of a vector quantized variational autoencoder was analyzed. In terms of error classification, four different model architectures were evaluated. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of anomaly detection and confirm that deep learning models can distinguish between multiple error categories beyond traditional binary classification. This extends the capabilities of conventional monitoring approaches, achieving accuracies of up to 100%. Additionally, real-world data material was examined in order to further demonstrate model robustness. Overall the results indicate strong generalization capability and highlight the practical potential of the developed models for use in industrial screwdriving processes, eliminating the need for expert knowledge in error identification and significantly reducing manual effort and analysis time.

### [353] [Detection Is Not Early Warning: Evaluating Token-Level Alarms on Language Model Failures](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16803)
*Marco De Negri,Luca Sartori,Lorenzo Baggi,Moritz Reihs,Eduard Frank Ďurech,Mennatallah El-Assady,Valentina Pyatkin,Anna Hedström*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Many failures of language models begin at a specific token, the onset. A monitor that reads the model during generation can classify the finished response, detect the failure once it is under way, or warn before it begins, and only a warning leaves time to stop or steer the generation. Monitors are usually evaluated with response-level metrics such as AUROC, which ignore when the monitor fires. We introduce PREWARN, an evaluation protocol for any failure with an annotated onset. It calibrates each monitor's threshold on validation data to an error rate chosen for the application, runs the monitor, and scores its alarms relative to the onset on all three tasks. As a case study we apply it to repetitive degeneration in three open language models, with early warning as the main task, using linear probes on activations and six untrained baselines. Response-level metrics saturate on this failure, and a rule that reads only the response length scores almost perfectly, while probes that AUROC ranks as equal warn very differently under PREWARN. Probes warn before the onset on most degenerate responses of two of the three models, low-rank adapters below the probe more than double the share of tokens just before the onset that it flags, largely by flagging degenerate responses long before the onset, and no untrained baseline warns much more often than random alarms. We release the probes with calibrated thresholds at this https URL

### [354] [Calibration and Conformal Prediction for Medical Question Answering in Arabic and English: Evidence from Two Non-Parallel Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16821)
*Mariya*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly tested on medical exam questions, but accuracy alone does not show when an answer can be trusted. I study the calibration and uncertainty of two open-weight models, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Jais-adapted-7B-chat (both run in 4-bit precision), on 2,816 English multiple-choice questions from MedMCQA and 4,927 Arabic multiple-choice questions from MedAraBench. Accuracy was 0.561 (English) and 0.430 (Arabic) for Qwen, and 0.369 and 0.308 for Jais. Raw option probabilities were overconfident in all four settings (expected calibration error 0.242 to 0.486), and a single temperature parameter removed 82% to 93% of that error. Split conformal prediction reached its nominal coverage in all 24 settings I tested (within 0.006), but the sets were large when accuracy was low: at 90% coverage, temperature-scaled sets contained on average 63% (Qwen, English), 78% (Qwen, Arabic), 86% (Jais, English) and 89% (Jais, Arabic) of the options. The margin between the top two option probabilities separated correct from incorrect answers best for Qwen on English (AUROC 0.734) and worst for Jais on Arabic (0.579). Answering only the 20% most confident questions lowered Qwen's English error from 0.439 to 0.098. Jais showed a strong prior for option C (49% of English and 60% of Arabic predictions). Scoring Latin letters only cut the Arabic share to 29% but left accuracy, raw ECE and AUROC nearly unchanged. Because the two benchmarks differ in subject, level and number of options, I do not attribute differences between languages to language itself. Code is available at this https URL .

### [355] [Sustainable Federated Fine-Tuning with LoRA: Environmental Impact and Performance Footprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16856)
*Pedro Augusto Londe Ribeiro,Rodrigo Moreira,Larissa Ferreira Rodrigues Moreira,Joberto S. B. Martins,Tereza C. Carvalho,Flávio de Oliveira Silva*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Federated Learning (FL) with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) enables efficient adaptation of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet its energy and carbon costs across hardware remain poorly understood. We evaluated federated Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning on NVIDIA A40, RTX 6000 Ada, and A100 GPUs using a $2^2$ full factorial design with 135M/360M models and 10/100 local steps. CodeCarbon tracked energy and estimated CO$_2$-equivalent emissions. Descriptive allocation of variation assigned 84.8-91.2% of energy and emissions variation to local steps within these ranges. On A40 and RTX 6000 Ada, configurations with fewer steps achieved comparable accuracy with roughly 6-8-fold lower energy consumption and higher accuracy per kWh. These findings support smaller local budgets for energy-efficient federated fine-tuning within the evaluated setting.

### [356] [Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16905)
*Jaemyung Yu,Byeongho Heo,Sangdoo Yun,Dongyoon Han*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Second-order optimizers (e.g., Shampoo, SOAP) have emerged as compelling alternatives to Adam/AdamW and promise faster per-step convergence than AdamW in transformer training. However, they still remain costly in practice, and even SOAP still pays substantial optimizer-state memory and eigendecomposition overhead. We ask whether the benefits of SOAP can be retained at nearly the efficiency of AdamW. In this paper, we answer yes with a lightweight SOAP variant, Factored One-sided Adam-Moment (FOAM). The path to practical impact is twofold: first, FOAM employs input-only preconditioning, dropping the output-side Kronecker factor to reduce memory and remove one eigendecomposition. The Kronecker structure of the Hessian shows that this is exact for a diagonal output-side curvature and nearly lossless for a near-diagonal one, as we observe empirically. Second, FOAM replaces SOAP's dense rotated second moment with a factored Adam-moment estimator based on row-by-column statistics. Under the K-FAC Fisher assumption with a diagonal output curvature, this estimator exactly recovers SOAP's dense second moment, and we measure only a 15-20% K-FAC violation, with negligible effect on the update. Our empirical results support the claim that FOAM matches strong SOAP and Muon baselines in validation loss across scales of large language model (LLM) pre-training, uses half of SOAP's optimizer state, runs at Muon-class wall-clock time, and retains robustness across a three-fold learning-rate range. The results hold from 124M to 760M parameters, demonstrating that SOAP's gains need not require SOAP's cost. Code: this https URL

### [357] [Time Flies When You Parallelise: Pareto-efficient Time Series Foundation Models with Linear Recurrences](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16934)
*Torben Berndt,Lingyi Yang,Federico Nardi,Yi Heng Lim,AJ Shears,Benjamin Walker*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Time series foundation models have demonstrated strong zero-shot forecasting performance, but computational efficiency remains a central architectural challenge. Temporal self-attention incurs quadratic cost in the number of temporal tokens, while nonlinear recurrent state transitions restrict parallel computation along the temporal dimension. We introduce ci-proto, a family of time series foundation models based on Mamba-3, whose linear state recurrences support chunk-wise parallel-in-time computation during training, and inference costs that scale linearly with sequence length. The architecture alternates recurrent temporal processing with cross-variate attention, supporting multivariate probabilistic forecasting with past-only and future-known covariates. Across fev-bench's 100 forecasting tasks, ci-proto XL sets a new state of the art among time series foundation models. The five ci-proto variants also make up the entire Pareto frontier for mean scaled quantile loss and mean absolute scaled error against both parameter count and median runtime.

### [358] [Temporal Regularized Learning: Self-Supervised Learning Local in Space and Time](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17019)
*Davide Wiest*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Layer-local self-supervised objectives remove the backward pass between layers, but almost all still compute their loss over a batch of samples and are therefore local in space but not in time. We introduce Temporal Regularized Learning (TeReL), a spatially and temporally local learning rule for self-supervised representation learning from sequential input streams. The key idea is to instantiate a VICReg-style objective with temporally adjacent positives and non-differentiated running population statistics, yielding a per-neuron online loss with bounded state. The objective is a soft form of Slow Feature Analysis, and its gradient is a Hebbian update of the feedforward weights and an anti-Hebbian update of one lateral matrix per layer. The aim of the experiments is to show that the rule works in a small network, not to compete with backpropagation. On a class-chunked MNIST stream, a two-layer fully connected network trained with batch size one outperforms random features (96.48% versus 95.09% linear-probe accuracy) and classical SFA, and a variant that relaxes both locality constraints is comparable to supervised backpropagation. Because training and inference use the same computation, the network can keep learning from unlabeled data during inference without loss of accuracy.

Abstract: Layer-local self-supervised objectives remove the backward pass between layers, but almost all still compute their loss over a batch of samples and are therefore local in space but not in time. We introduce Temporal Regularized Learning (TeReL), a spatially and temporally local learning rule for self-supervised representation learning from sequential input streams. The key idea is to instantiate a VICReg-style objective with temporally adjacent positives and non-differentiated running population statistics, yielding a per-neuron online loss with bounded state. The objective is a soft form of Slow Feature Analysis, and its gradient is a Hebbian update of the feedforward weights and an anti-Hebbian update of one lateral matrix per layer. The aim of the experiments is to show that the rule works in a small network, not to compete with backpropagation. On a class-chunked MNIST stream, a two-layer fully connected network trained with batch size one outperforms random features (96.48% versus 95.09% linear-probe accuracy) and classical SFA, and a variant that relaxes both locality constraints is comparable to supervised backpropagation. Because training and inference use the same computation, the network can keep learning from unlabeled data during inference without loss of accuracy.

### [359] [Capacity-Constrained Delayed Feedback for Online Conformal Risk Control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17059)
*Bowen Wang,Osvaldo Simeone*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Online conformal risk control (OCRC) enables reliable uncertainty quantification in machine learning by converting model outputs into prediction sets with long-term risk guarantees. These guarantees, however, hinge on the assumption that the loss of each round is revealed immediately and losslessly. In practice, feedback may be delayed, and limited resources may prevent tracking all pending predictions, causing some feedback to be lost. To address this challenge, we develop capacity-aware OCRC (CA-OCRC), a framework that jointly determines how to allocate limited tracking feedback capacity and how to construct prediction sets. CA-OCRC is based on a randomized tracking policy that samples a proxy delay to decide whether, and for how long, feedback for the current round is tracked. CA-OCRC updates the prediction sets via inverse probability weighting, compensating for the possibility of feedback lost due to delays and limited tracking capacity. We analyze risk bounds for both arbitrary and stochastic delays, revealing a trade-off between receiving more feedback and avoiding capacity saturation. Building on these bounds, we optimize the proxy delay distribution, showing scaling laws for the tracking capacity that ensure the same long-term risk as OCRC with unlimited feedback. Experiments on medical imaging, natural language processing, computer vision, and wireless communications show the effectiveness of CA-OCRC as compared to existing OCRC mechanisms.

### [360] [LazyWeights: Decode-on-Demand Edge LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17108)
*Arnab Sanyal,Gourav Datta,Sandeep P. Chinchali*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Memory decides which LLMs an edge device runs, and how fast: capacity on a $4$ GB Jetson Nano, bandwidth on an $8$ GB Jetson Orin Nano Super. Deployed formats (GPTQ, AWQ, $\texttt{ this http URL }$'s K- and I-quants) spend equal bits on every integer code of a matrix, although the codes are far from uniform. $\texttt{LazyWeights}$ keeps these formats but tunes GPTQ so the codes compress, Huffman-codes them losslessly in interleaved lanes, and decodes them on demand in a small unit between DRAM and L2, so GPU kernels run unchanged and DRAM moves only coded bytes. At $1\%$ and $3.5\%$ perplexity budgets, coded Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B and SmolLM-1.7B are $5.7-31.4\%$ smaller than the best $\texttt{ this http URL }$ format. A bit-exact $0.21$ mm$^2$ ASIC decoder unit ($1$ GHz, $7$ nm) cuts Orin latency and energy per token by up to $36\%$ and $38\%$ ($54\%$ and $44\%$ with prompt-lookup speculation). On the Nano, $\texttt{LazyWeights}$ needs $58-64\%$ less time and $53-57\%$ less energy per token than CPU $\texttt{ this http URL }$, and runs a streamed Mistral-7B 6.6$\times$ faster at $3.89$ bits per weight. A Huffman decoder beats an rANS decoder in rate and area at equal throughput; the ASIC decoder unit runs bit-exact on a Zynq UltraScale+ FPGA (AMD ZCU102).

### [361] [Near-Optimal Regret for Oracle-Efficient Adversarial Contextual Bandits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17109)
*Kiarash Banihashem,MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: We study contextual bandits with $K$ actions, a class of $N$ policies, and i.i.d.\ contexts from a distribution that the learner can sample. For any sequence of loss functions fixed before play, we give an oracle-efficient algorithm with expected regret $O(\sqrt{KT\log(2N)}\,\log(2KT))$ against the best policy in hindsight on the realized contexts. This improves the $T^{2/3}$ dependence on the horizon in prior oracle-efficient bounds and achieves the optimal regret rate in this setting up to logarithmic factors. Our algorithm perturbs policy scores using a Poisson sample of auxiliary contexts. At each sampled context, the perturbation assigned to an action is a Laplace noise draw multiplied by a scale specific to that context and action. We show that choosing these scales to minimize a convex objective determined by past observations yields the stated regret bound. We further approximate the minimizing scales by projected stochastic gradient descent using only an exact offline cost-sensitive optimization oracle that returns the optimum value. Since the table of scales can be large, the algorithm represents the SGD iterates implicitly by storing the random draws that determine each update and evaluates the scales only at queried contexts. Both the oracle complexity and the remaining resource bounds are polynomial in $T$, $K$, and $\log(2N)$.

### [362] [Bellman Contraction under MMD: A Unified Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17116)
*Baptiste Debes,Tinne Tuytelaars*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: We introduce a mathematical framework for studying contraction of the distributional Bellman operator under Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD). We show that contraction reduces to conditional positive definiteness of an associated kernel constructed from the base kernel, which we call the Bellman difference kernel. Focusing on radial kernels, we use Schoenberg's theorem to connect this condition to Bernstein functions. This gives contraction criteria that hold in any dimension and can be verified analytically or tested numerically. Our framework unifies known results for the Gaussian RBF, power-distance, and multiquadric kernels. A numerical search identifies 11 new kernels that induce contraction. We also propose chaining, a general construction that produces kernels inducing contraction with any prescribed factor. To reconcile theory with practice, we show that contraction on a set only requires conditional positive definiteness on that set. This explains why the RBF kernel can remain a valid choice when rewards are bounded, despite its lack of global contraction. Finally, we identify a fundamental tradeoff between contraction rate and discriminative power, where kernels that contract faster tend to discriminate less between distributions. Code is available at this https URL

### [363] [Using an energy pixels approach to estimate the size a 2nd Generation DEL must be to train a high-resolution binding model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17121)
*Boris P. Belotserkovskii,R. Edward Watts*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) are commonly used to find small-molecule binders to a target protein. But the hard part is no longer finding a hit. It is building a machine-learning model good enough to guide the medicinal chemistry that follows, one that can resolve the shift in affinity when a chemist changes a single atom. Such a model needs two things from its training data: dense sampling of the small patch of chemical space around the hit, and an adequate number of genuinely tight binders within it. A diverse naive DEL gives neither. It samples an enormous space, so any one neighborhood is covered far too thinly, and the tightest binders are rare. A model trained on that naive DEL data must extrapolate to binders tighter than any it has seen, and that is where models can fail. One way to get training data with both properties is a second-generation DEL built around the hit. We ask how complex that library must be. We treat binding as a sum of small, independent interactions, called pixels on the target and antipixels on the ligand. From the spread of affinities measured in the naive library, with no structural information and nothing yet synthesized, we estimate the complexity such a library must have to supply that dense sampling and those tight binders. The method does two useful things. It turns the number of tight binders a model needs into the number of compounds a library must contain. And it estimates the expected yield of a randomly designed second-generation DEL, so the gain from designing the library with machine learning or active learning can be measured against a baseline, without the expense of a control library as large as the experiment itself.

### [364] [Support-Constrained Offline Policy Improvement for Pediatric ECMO from Limited Clinical Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17134)
*Fateme Golivand Darvishvand,Saurabh Mathur,Nikhilesh Prabhakar,Michael A. Skinner,Ameet Soni,Neel Shah,Ethan L Sanford,Lakshmi Raman,Sriraam Natarajan*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Managing children on ECMO (Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation) requires balancing short-term physiological stability with the long-term goal of preventing neurological injury. Standard reinforcement learning can propose risky, out-of-distribution actions, while imitation learning is limited to reproducing clinician behavior. We introduce Support-Constrained Fitted Q-Iteration (FQI-SC), an offline reinforcement learning framework that cautiously improves upon expert behavior by restricting optimization to empirically supported state-action pairs and defaulting to the clinician baseline in low-data regions. On 78 pediatric trajectories totaling over 6,000 hours of clinical data, we evaluate our framework using Fitted Q-Evaluation (FQE) and a behavioral disagreement. Additionally, we formalize the performance-safety trade-off by introducing a unified Balance Score ($S(\pi)$). Our empirical evaluation shows that support-constrained policy improves the Balance Score by 38\% relative to FQI, improves estimated value by 1.28 FQE units over imitation learning, and reduces disagreement with clinician actions by 71\% relative to FQI.

### [365] [ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17141)
*Peter Sharpe*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: A foundational principle of physics is that all coordinate systems are equally valid: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the origin or orientation of the frame, nor on the units or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet the neural surrogates with the lowest errors on today's aerodynamics benchmarks lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation) and from one mesher, rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs in which no learned operation receives a coordinate and every sum over the boundary is a quadrature. Positions enter only as distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors, lengths are measured in a unit computed from the boundary, and interior points query the boundary through a tree-accelerated learned kernel without influencing one another. With every boundary cell a token and an exact boundary read, ISLA is equivariant to rigid motions and reflections, invariant to the units of its declared data, and consistent under mesh refinement, while at every setting each query is independent of all other queries. On AeroZoo, 2,816 flows that vary in shape, size, speed, and boundary conditions, its mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 3.1 and 3.3 times lower than any baseline's. On AirfRANS its errors are second only to those of a boundary-integral model (GLOBE) and at least 1.6 times lower than those of Transolver and GeoTransolver.

### [366] [A Convex-Analytic Reformulation for Poisoning Attacks on Logistic Regression](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17143)
*Carina Moreira Costa,Maria Eduarda Pinheiro,Martin Schmidt*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: We study data poisoning attacks on logistic regression with $\ell_2$-regularization, where an attacker chooses the features of a fixed number of injected observations with prescribed labels to maximize the logistic loss on the clean training data. Strong convexity of the defender's problem yields an exact reformulation through its first-order optimality conditions. Using convex conjugacy of the softplus function, we replace the sigmoid relations by a single convex optimality-gap inequality and express the attacker's objective as a concave function. A change of variables makes the stationarity condition affine, leaving bounded bilinear equalities as the only nonconvex constraints. We derive finite bounds on all variables involved in these equalities, including a global bound on the coefficient norm and tighter bounds obtained by preprocessing based on convex optimization. Experiments on eight binary classification datasets evaluate attack effectiveness and compare the two reformulations when solved with \textsf{SCIP}. Attacks obtained by local optimization degrade predictive performance on most datasets, while the convex-analytic formulation produces substantially stronger reported dual bounds within a fixed time limit.

### [367] [Enhancing Preference Detection using Eye Movement Cascade and Multilayer Combinatorial Fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17145)
*Yuanhong Wu,Mary Tsaryk,Sam Watson,Tahsin Ahmed,Christina Schweikert,D. Frank Hsu*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Understanding how visual attention influences human preference formation is a fundamental problem in consumer behavior and cognitive science. In this work, we investigate how eye movement patterns can be used to predict preference decisions when subjects compare two alternatives. To address this problem, we analyze an eye-tracking dataset, where subjects view pairs of face images and their gaze behavior is recorded throughout the decision process. We model this problem using multiple machine learning classifiers and apply the Multi-layer Combinatorial Fusion (MCF) framework to iteratively combine diverse models. The MCF framework expands models to a large pool of model fusions and then reduces them based on cognitive diversity, repeating this process across layers until diversity diminishes. Experimental results show that MCF significantly improves performance over individual models. The best single model achieves a Pre@k of 0.90, which is improved to 0.9143 after the first layer of MCF, and further increased to 0.9286 in the second layer. This progression demonstrates that the second layer not only surpasses the performance of the first layer but also outperforms the best individual model, highlighting the effectiveness of leveraging diversity through multi-layer fusion.

### [368] [AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17152)
*Peter Sharpe,Carmelo Gonzales,Corey Adams,Mehdi Ataei,Sanjay Choudhry*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Neural surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are trained and ranked on datasets that each vary one design family in one flow domain. Such datasets cannot test the least that an aerodynamic foundation model must do: predict CFD-quality incompressible flow in seconds for new shapes in new enclosures. On DrivAerML, larger models and longer training barely lower Transolver's error; doubling the training cases cuts it by about 12% up to 400 cases, exhausting the dataset. We introduce AeroZoo, a benchmark and training corpus of 3,815 time-mean solutions to the unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) equations with a transition model, across seven geometry families, eight enclosure configurations and Reynolds numbers from $10^3$ to $10^8$. Each sample poses a well-posed PDE problem in the form a solver receives it: the boundary meshes grouped by condition type, the prescribed values and the fluid properties. The 2,816 samples with a stable time mean form the canonical benchmark: two tasks, engineering metrics and 22 frozen splits, disjoint in geometry, that hold out geometry families, enclosures, boundary-condition layouts and Reynolds ranges. On the random split, boundary-condition tokens cut GeoTransolver's median velocity error from 76.9% to 8.4% of the inlet speed in single-seed runs (uniform inlet flow: 11.0%). ISLA, a transformer for boundary-driven PDEs, reaches 5.3% over four seeds, about 4 times the change from a finer mesh. On the same test samples, a held-out geometry family barely changes ISLA's error relative to uniform flow, and a held-out enclosure or boundary-condition layout raises it 2.4 to 9.2 times. The data and the scoring code will be released.

On the random split, boundary-condition tokens cut GeoTransolver's median velocity error from 76.9% to 8.4% of the inlet speed in single-seed runs (uniform inlet flow: 11.0%). ISLA, a transformer for boundary-driven PDEs, reaches 5.3% over four seeds, about 4 times the change from a finer mesh. On the same test samples, a held-out geometry family barely changes ISLA's error relative to uniform flow, and a held-out enclosure or boundary-condition layout raises it 2.4 to 9.2 times. The data and the scoring code will be released.

</details>


### [369] [Symmetry in Time: A Representation Theory of Linear Recurrent Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17162)
*Anif N. Shikder,Ramit Dey,Jan Minac,Lyle E. Muller*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: State space models (SSMs) are an emerging alternative to Transformers. SSMs offer linear-time inference and parallel training, but most implementations make the parallel scan efficient by making the recurrence diagonal: each channel of the hidden state is multiplied by an input-dependent real or complex number. These numbers commute, so the state records which inputs occurred but not their order. We formalize this with representation theory, which explains and fixes the state-tracking failures previously reported for SSMs. The state update defines a linear representation of the monoid of input sequences, and we show that an SSM tracks a group at every sequence length exactly when that group is a quotient of the group generated by its transition matrices. Two consequences follow. Diagonal real- and complex-valued SSMs can track only commutative groups, while the transition matrices of any SSM that can track a group must split into independent blocks over the real, complex, and quaternion numbers. We then introduce HyperSSM, which adds quaternion channels while keeping linear-time inference and parallel training. Trained only on final answers, HyperSSM solves the group tasks of recent state-tracking benchmarks exactly with at most five state numbers. This includes $S_5$ with 32 generators, where previous SSMs are at chance, and HyperSSM generalizes to sequences 25 times longer than those seen in training. Because the theory says what the transitions must encode, the learned weights of the linear recurrence can be interpreted directly. We demonstrate this by recovering the calibration of a real gyroscope, the rotations of imperfect qubit gates and the geometry of protein backbones.

### [370] [Maximizing Capacity Utilization of LoRA Adapters for Mitigating the Learning-Forgetting Trade-off](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17191)
*Tomohiro Sawada,Kartik Goyal*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) often underperforms full fine-tuning, especially in heterogeneous and continual-learning settings in which substantial forgetting occurs. In general, it suffers from an undesirable learning-forgetting trade-off across diverse fine-tuning settings. We identify a potential contributor: LoRA adapters, especially high-rank ones, frequently fail to realize the available capacity afforded by the configured rank. Specifically, we find that standard LoRA updates have effective rank far below their configured rank, limiting how broadly the update energy is distributed. Therefore, we propose training mechanisms that optimize the original objective while maximizing adapter effective rank. Our main method adds a simple, stable, differentiable, and SVD-free Rényi-2 effective-rank regularizer to the language-modeling loss. We also connect capacity maximization to norm-bounded updates. In mixed-domain rank sweeps on three models evaluated with multiple random seeds, a penalty weight of $\lambda=0.01$ lowers mean Wiki perplexity at every tested rank of at least $16$ relative to unpenalized LoRA. Mean training perplexity improves or increases by at most $0.02$ in all but one model-rank comparison. Single-task and scheduling experiments further show that the balance between learning and retention depends on the configuration. We also observe that several LoRA variants in the literature also suffer from the identified capacity issue, and our approach provides a complementary axis of improvement to LoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning. These results suggest that effective rank is not only a post-hoc diagnostic of adapter quality, but a trainable objective for improving the learning-forgetting frontier. Our code is available at this https URL

### [371] [Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17196)
*Lucy Liu,Leon M. Kamp,Katia Bertoldi,L. Mahadevan*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Automatic differentiation has enabled rapid progress on continuous-variable mechanical design problems, but gradient-based optimization still struggles with discrete variables. The standard approach is to optimize using a continuous relaxation of the choices, then commit to the nearest discrete design at the end. Why this procedure selects unfavorable basins is poorly understood. Here, we introduce a practical, interpretable design problem inspired by origami, in which automatic differentiation is used to design shapes with a target functional behavior. Each origami sheet has a fixed geometry, and a bilevel optimization framework tunes which one of four discrete hinge types to place at each fold. Baseline gradient-based design settles into basins with a large discretization gap: relaxed optimization solves 97% of runs, but the final, discrete solutions succeed only half the time. We find that the gap can be relieved with a surprisingly simple modification. An initialization prior uniformly biased toward the stiff, flat hinge option boosts the final solve fraction from 49% to 69%. Applying the prior adds no additional compute and leaves the optimization process unchanged. Compared to the baseline, sheets produced with the prior have greater geometric compatibility and mechanical stiffness. Directly penalizing frustration and floppiness in the outer loss function produces an even greater improvement than the prior does, raising the solve fraction to 78% and indicating that these properties help distinguish the unfavorable basins. Our results demonstrate that loss landscapes for mechanical design can have physically meaningful basins that are not robust to discretization and cause solves to fail. Targeting these basins' physical signatures, even with just an initialization bias, helps avoid them.

### [372] [Two mathematical models of knowledge distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17230)
*Audrey Xie,Ludwig Schmidt,John Duchi*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Many hypotheses compete to explain the successes of knowledge distillation. To help address this, we propose and analyze a mathematical model of distillation, which suggests that distillation's performance comes not from obtaining better models but from easier to optimize landscapes. For generalized linear models trained with stochastic gradient descent, we prove that distillation fits performant student models asymptotically more quickly than non-distilled models. In rank-1 matrix approximation, we characterize conditions on the target matrix under which gradient descent with distillation converges strictly faster than training on the supervised objective. The theory helps delineate the ways distillation provides benefits (i.e., in optimization speed, not in generalization), and experiments on real datasets corroborate the theoretical predictions.

### [373] [Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17287)
*Jiacheng Xu,Shuo He,Fuxiang Zhang,Chaojie Wang,Bo An*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) typically relies on a verifier that can reliably judge whether sampled solutions are correct. However, in many realistic settings, complete verification is generally unavailable, while cheap checks can only falsify failures. We formalize this regime as one-sided verifiability (OSV): verified negatives are reliable counterexamples, but verified positives are merely non-falsified candidates and may contain many false positives. This asymmetry makes standard RLVR unreliable, because reinforcing verified positives can directly reward shortcuts that pass partial checks. To address this issue, we propose Negative-Only Policy Optimization (NOPO), which treats verified positives as unlabeled and updates the policy only by suppressing trusted verified negatives. Specifically, NOPO combines a reference-relative negative suppression loss with a group-level adapter that scales each update by the proportion of non-falsified responses. Across unit-test, constraint-check, and LLM self-verifiers, NOPO improves pass@k over baselines on code, logic, and math benchmarks when oracle rewards are unavailable. These gains persist under inference-time scaling and cross-benchmark transfer.

### [374] [Towards a Theory of Learnability via Debate](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17303)
*Tosca Lechner,Vinayak Pathak,Sivan Sabato,Ruth Urner*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Debate has been recently proposed as a training protocol that is hoped to produce more aligned models even as model capabilities scale. The idea is that the human, instead of providing supervision in the form of labels, judges a debate between two models that compete to prove the correctness of opposite labels. It can be shown that functions of a much higher computational complexity can be correctly judged in this way, compared to the complexity of functions that can be directly evaluated using a computationally weak evaluator. This suggests that perhaps debate can be used to teach very complicated functions to models. However, previous work has largely ignored the fact that this is a training protocol, and simply analyzes the game being played between the two debaters for a known judge. We take the first steps towards understanding the learning problem implicit within the protocol, by formulating it as an online learning problem. We show that once we formulate the learning problem precisely, there are cases where the best way to learn given access to a judge is different from running an adversarial debate. This motivates us to define a cooperative version of the protocol, whose learnability we characterize using a combinatorial dimension. We also consider the possibility of the human judge being fallible and occasionally judging the debate incorrectly. We show that a small number of errors in judgement can lead to a large error in learning.

### [375] [Linking Rapid Learning to Compositional Structure in Neural Networks: Evidence from Additive Analogies in Meta-Learned Parameter Spaces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17314)
*Abigail L. Tenenbaum,R. Thomas McCoy*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Humans can learn rapidly from limited experience, while neural networks typically require extensive training. In this work, we investigate what properties of a neural network can enable it to learn rapidly. We study neural networks that have been optimized via meta-learning, a technique that exposes a network to many related functions to facilitate its subsequent learning of similar functions. Prior work has shown that these meta-learned networks can learn new functions rapidly, but how they do so remains unclear. To investigate their internal structure, we take inspiration from classic work demonstrating additive relationships among the learned vectors that neural networks use to represent words (e.g., "king" minus "man" plus "woman" approximates "queen"). Analogously, we look for additive relationships among a meta-learned network's "representations" of different functions; when a meta-learned network rapidly learns to implement a specific function, all of its adapted parameter values can be concatenated into a single vector that we treat as representing the function. We find that such parameter vectors can be added and subtracted according to symbolic relationships among the functions they represent, yielding new parameter vectors that successfully represent the functions predicted by the corresponding symbolic manipulations: the networks specified by these artificially recombined vectors actually implement the intended functions without any direct training on them. Our results suggest that meta-learning can tune a network's starting point to organize subsequent learning along systematic, functionally meaningful trajectories through the space of possible parameter vectors, providing a geometric basis for realizing inductive biases in neural networks.

### [376] [Internalizing Investment Mandates: A Neurosymbolic RL Approach to Portfolio Allocation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17329)
*Zeynep Yıldız,Satchit Chatterji,Ercan Atam,Erman Acar*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Institutional portfolios operate under investment policy statements that specify asset allocation constraints, often conditioned on market regime information. Deep reinforcement learning has been shown to optimize financial performance but typically does not enforce rule compliance, making it unsuitable for real-world deployment. Existing neurosymbolic methods such as Probabilistic Logic Policy Gradient (PLPG) offer constraint-satisfying reinforcement learning (RL) via differentiable symbolic supervision but assume a finite, discrete action space. We present a PLPG-inspired continuous allocation method that estimates the probability that the policy's own executed action satisfies the investment mandate, using reparameterized Monte Carlo sampling, and adds it to the training objective. No post-hoc enforcement mechanism intercepts actions at inference time and compliance is learned by the agent. Audited directly on deterministic mean actions with no correction, the policy reduces violations of a six-rule regime-conditional mandate from 96-98% for unconstrained RL and 33.4% for a reward-penalty baseline to 4.8%, showing that a continuous-action neurosymbolic policy can substantially internalize a symbolic mandate.

### [377] [CuEVM: Scaling Smart Contract Execution on GPUs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14916)
*Nhut-Minh Ho,Tien Tuan Anh Dinh,Quang Trung Ta,Fredrik Svantes,Xiaokui Xiao,Beng Chin Ooi*

Main category: cs.DC

TL;DR: CuEVM 是一个完全运行在 GPU 上、语义完备的以太坊虚拟机（EVM）执行引擎，将交易执行视为大规模并行的数据处理问题；配套的 CuEVM-fuzz 是首个把整个模糊测试循环迁移到 GPU 的智能合约 fuzzer，在单张消费级 GPU 上达到约 830 万 TPS（ERC-20）与 110 万次/秒端到端模糊测试执行，超越现有基线最高两个数量级，并在 115 个真实合约中发现高危漏洞。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: EVM 逐笔串行执行交易，成为区块链吞吐瓶颈，尤其限制了那些交易之间大多互不冲突、可并行执行的新兴负载（交易仿真、乐观调度的区块重执行、覆盖率引导的智能合约模糊测试、安全事件响应）。已有 GPU 方案 MAU 语义不完备：它把字节码转译为 PTX 模拟执行，只支持 EVM 语义子集，缺失外部调用、预编译合约、合约创建与回滚，且世界状态被限制为单一合约，超过 80% 的官方测试失败，必须回退到 CPU 参考 EVM，从而重新引入串行瓶颈；同时其按线程分离的覆盖率缓冲区带来高开销。另一方面，GPU 程序对内存访问模式与线程分歧极为敏感，需精心设计数据布局与调度以降低访存延迟与主机—设备通信开销。

Method: 核心引擎：按以太坊黄皮书实现完整 EVM 语义，全部 opcode 以实例函数形式在 GPU 上执行，含 gas meter、从零实现的 256 位算术库（改编自 CGBN）、Shanghai 版全部预编译合约与哈希函数；采用列式（struct-of-arrays）内存布局，将所有实例的同字段连续存放以实现合并访存，动态结构（栈、内存、calldata）以列式缓冲+每实例偏移表示，调用深度维度被扁平化进同一缓冲区（stack = ⟨base_ptr, offset, dyn_ptr, size⟩，子调用 offset = min(offset+size, buffer_size)）以避免按 1024 深度×k 物化张量；世界状态按列式预分配（x 账户 × y 存储槽），存储值含 v_curr/v_org/v_warm 以正确计费；回滚采用乐观 undo log（写入直接生效并记录日志，revert 时逆序重放），避免每次调用的快照/版本开销。执行模型为 shared-nothing 分区：批次含 N 条序列、每序列 M 笔交易，由 M 个 kernel 推进；主机仅在批次边界（每轮一次双向）传输数据；引擎暴露调度接口，让主机把控制流相似的事务分组到同一 warp（每个 warp 一个合约函数）。应用层 CuEVM-fuzz：GPU 常驻三个模块——类型感知的变异器（按字节码中 ABI 类型标注可变参数 Γ=⟨seed,[(offset,type,length)]⟩，用 AFL 式变异）、覆盖率跟踪（2^16 字，分支距离 8 位+命中计数 24 位，eid=(pc≪1 ⊕ pc_dst)⊕a，用 atomic add/atomic max 实现并发生命周期与距离反馈）、漏洞 oracle；共享覆盖率与 oracle 缓冲区用 CUDA 原子操作而非锁，私有结果缓冲最后用 atomic 索引聚合到共享输出；CPU 控制器基于 Medusa，引入 Slither 的函数依赖信息（F_dep/F_infl）生成状态相关序列；主机—设备流量最小化：配置与世界状态快照常驻 GPU，每 warp 只传一个索引加基础种子，CPU 侧复现同样的伪随机发生器以重建有趣序列，避免回传变异数据。

Result: 正确性：通过 GoEVMLab 与 Geth 对比 EIP-3155 trace（gas 与每条指令完整栈），VMTests 通过率 100%，全量执行测试 96.2%（失败多为接近调用深度上限的 revert 边界处 gas 差异与 trace 打印超时）；MAU 在放宽校验下仅通过 18.7%。吞吐：ERC-20 达 8.3M TPS（512k 线程，占约 24.9GB），Uniswap 类含大量外部调用约 441k TPS，相比 Geth/RETH/PEVM 最高提升两个数量级。扩展性：16k→512k 线程近线性增长，ERC-20 受显存容量限制，Uniswap 在 128k 线程后因动态内存争用略降。模糊测试：端到端达 1.1M 次/秒，比最优 CPU 基线 Medusa 快 23×、比 GPU 基线 MAU 快 4.8×；前两秒即取得最佳指令覆盖，比 MAU 多 4% 覆盖且时间短 30×；LabeledDataset 上 2 秒报出 51 个 CVE（Smartian 需 10 分钟），RE 假阳性与 ItyFuzz 同为 18 个真阳性；EtherScan500 上找到 295 IB、8 LE、20 AC、10 RE（Smartian 169 IB/4 LE，ItyFuzz 18 AC/6 RE），即 1.75× 更多 IB、2× 更多 LE、1.67× 更多 RE；PopularContract（Ethereum 与 BSC 各 10,000 合约、每合约 10 秒预算）在 115 个合约中发现高危漏洞（42 ETH + 73 BSC：89 IB、11 RE、9 AC，其余 LE），对比 ItyFuzz 仅 18 个项目且假阳性 256/274；已开展 best-effort 负责任披露，三个团队确认。消融：no_sched/no_mem 变体性能显著下降（no_mem 最差），说明内存预分配与合并访存最关键；CPU-only 变体在漏洞发现上大幅落后，证明 GPU 原生执行的必要性。事件响应原型 1 秒内找到比真实攻击交易多提取 9,000 USD（3.68 ETH）的 rescue 交易。

Conclusion: CuEVM 通过将 EVM 执行重构为批量数据并行负载，结合列式状态布局、GPU 感知调度与乐观回滚，实现了首个完全遵循 EVM 规范的 GPU 原生执行引擎，在保持语义完整性的同时把吞吐提升至 830 万 ERC-20 TPS 并随实例数扩展（瓶颈仍在 GPU 侧，暗示多 GPU 进一步加速空间）。CuEVM-fuzz 证明其可扩展到完整模糊测试循环（110 万次/秒、发现 115 个真实高危合约漏洞），事件响应应用进一步说明引擎的通用性。局限在于面向无冲突/分区隔离负载，跨分区可变共享状态需按用例处理；Uniswap 类深调用负载受动态内存争用限制；仍有 3.8% 官方测试因 gas 边界与打印限制未通过；误报主要源于 oracle 信息不完整。

Abstract: Smart contracts on Ethereum blockchain process transactions worth billions of US dollars daily. They run on top of Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) which executes transactions sequentially. This execution model creates a performance bottleneck, especially for new blockchain workloads with large numbers of transactions, such as security testing. We present CuEVM, a GPU-native and semantically complete EVM execution engine that treats transaction execution as a massively parallel data processing problem. It employs novel data structures and GPU-aware scheduling to accelerate execution. Unlike prior works that transpile the contract and rely on a host CPU for many operations, CuEVM supports complete EVM semantics natively on the GPU. It passes 100% of the Ethereum VMTests and 96.2% of the full execution-test suite. On a single commodity GPU, CuEVM executes over 8 million ERC-20 transfers per second, outperforming existing baselines by up to two orders of magnitude. We build a smart contract fuzzer, called CuEVM-fuzz, on top of CuEVM. The fuzzer achieves over a million end-to-end executions per second, up to 23x and 4.8x higher than the state-of-the-art CPU-based and GPU-based baselines, respectively.

</details>


### [378] [Reducing Batch Makespan for LLM Agent Workloads through Inference-Environment Coordination](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16661)
*Wei Feng,Meiling Chen,Boxiao Chen,Lu Liu,Bin Zi,Libin Ye,Xingyu Lu,Lei Xu,Jun Zhou*

Main category: cs.DC

TL;DR: 本文针对混合式 LLM 智能体工作负载提出一套"推理—环境协同"优化栈，包含四部分：基于工作负载的混合缓存（KV cache 与循环状态）容量模型与并发参考、负载有界一致性哈希路由（LBCH）、路由前缀调度（RP）、以及解耦样本准入与环境执行并引入链推进动作调度（CAAS）。在 Ling-3.0/3.1-Flash 与 BFCL、SWE-bench Multilingual、WideSearch、MCP-Atlas 上的实测显示批 makespan 降低 10.4%–65.0%，评测分数保持一致，并已用于 Ling-3.x 模型的训练与评测流程。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 智能体工作流（基准评测、合成数据生成、RL rollout）以"批次"方式执行，下游阶段需等待整批完成，因此批 makespan（完成批次所有样本的时间）而非传统服务关注的 TTFT/TPOT 直接决定模型研发迭代效率。由于每个智能体任务在 LLM 推理与环境交互之间交替，推理侧（缓存分配、路由、调度）与环境侧（执行并发、动作派发）任一环节成为瓶颈都会拖长批尾。具体痛点有三：(1) 混合模型（MLA + KDA，如 Ling-3.0-Flash）的 KV cache 与 recurrent state 分池存储，默认分配比例与目标工作负载不匹配时会出现一池耗尽、另一池闲置，限制可同时保留缓存的轨迹数；(2) 跨 worker 路由缺少"同一轨迹跨轮复用"的亲和性，但严格亲和又会造成负载倾斜；(3) 现有智能体框架（如 MCP-Atlas、τ³-bench）用单一并发限制耦合了样本准入与环境执行，环境容量低于推理能力时 GPU 空闲，且长链任务被推迟到批尾。

Method: 方法分为推理侧优化与推理—环境协同两部分，均在 SGLang 上实现。\n\n【推理侧】(1) 工作负载感知的混合缓存分配模型：设可用缓存显存为 M，比例 r = M_state/M_kv，得 M_state(r)=Mr/(1+r)、M_kv(r)=M/(1+r)；由历史轨迹画像估计每轨迹 KV 足迹 F_kv = L_kv·c_kv 与循环状态足迹 F_state = S_state·c_state（每轨迹仅保留最新一个 recurrent state），则联合驻留容量 C(r) = min{M_kv(r)/F_kv, M_state(r)/F_state}；令两池相等可解得平衡比 r^bal = F_state/F_kv = S_state·c_state/(L_kv·c_kv)，此时 C = M/(F_kv+F_state)。向下取整得每 worker 参考并发，W 个 worker 聚合为 C_I* = W·⌊C⌋；该比例在服务期固定，可选局部校准。\n\n【路由】负载有界一致性哈希 LBCH（Algorithm 1）：以轨迹标签 κ_k 哈希到一致性哈希环得 home worker，仅当 L(w) ≤ (L_tot+1)α/W（α≥1 为负载容忍因子）时选 home，否则沿环顺时针找首个合格后继，无合格则回落 home；只用标签与 in-flight 计数，不解析 prompt、不预测缓存内容。\n\n【调度】路由前缀调度 RP（Algorithm 2）：每 worker 维护容量 C_A 的轨迹标签 LRU 集合 A；等待队列中标签命中 A 的请求为第一层，查询 radix prefix cache 得命中长度 ℓ(q)（用 δ_q 标志避免重复查询并复用已记录值），优先级键 p(q) = (0, −ℓ(q), t_queue(q))；标签不在 A 的请求为第二层 (1, 0, t_queue(q))，跳过前缀查询以降低开销；按字典序升序排序后交由原生 BuildBatch 依资源约束组批。\n\n【推理—环境协同】(4) 容量分离：将样本准入上限 C_S 与环境执行上限 C_E 解耦，默认 C_S = C_I*、C_E 独立限制（对比传统统一门限 C_S^unified = min{C_I*, C_E}），使推理与环境阶段重叠。\n\n(5) 链推进动作调度 CAAS：环境作业在固定执行槽下按优先级键 p_E(j) = (g_j, −n_j, c_j, e_j) 派发，其中 g_j = ⌊a_j/B⌋ 为到达时间带、n_j 为已完成推理轮数（已揭示链深度）、c_j = ⌈τ̄_j/Δ_I⌉ 为观测平均推理时长的分桶、e_j 为全局递增序号；只用当轮观测进度，无需预知剩余长度，靠时间带防止深链反复插队早带作业。\n\n【评测框架】受控回放：真实推理 + 录制的环境响应与时长，固定 checkpoint、采样参数、任务集、硬件与提交顺序，用于逐项消融。

Result: 【受控回放】(1) 缓存与并发：模型导出的平衡比 r^bal 分别为 SWE 0.09、BFCL 2.26、WideSearch 0.10，参考并发 98/859/98；在这些工作点 makespan 已接近网格搜索最优。低并发下 makespan 对比例不敏感；高并发下比例失配会击穿复用——SWE C_S 147→157、BFCL 644→859、WideSearch 123→147 时缓存复用骤降、新 prefill 工作量升至约 11×/3×/9×，吞吐下降而 makespan 上升（SWE 甚至 6 小时超时）。(2) 调度：RP 在两个最高并发档均优于 FCFS、LPM、DFS-weight；缓存复用维持高位且新 prefill 增量小；优先级计算累计开销 SWE 303.05s vs LPM 735.00s / DFS 1704.25s，BFCL 10.91s（优于 LPM 7.65s 以外的两者），WideSearch 39.97s 最低；LPM 在 BFCL 因等待队列超 128 回退 FCFS 而开销低但丧失感知优先。(3) 路由：LBCH 在三工作负载上 makespan 最短，相对 CA 降 1.5%–13.6%、相对 CH 降 1.9%–3.8%；缓存复用率相近（SWE 98.4%–98.8%、BFCL 86.2%–87.2%、WideSearch 95.2%–95.7%），但请求数不平衡 β 与输出 token 不平衡 γ_out 明显更低，说明需联合考虑复用与负载均衡。(4) 协同：容量分离把统一门限提到 C_S=10 即降约 1/3 makespan，继续提高收益递减（受环境释放能力限制）；CAAS 相对 FCFS 在 C_E=3/5 时 makespan 再降 1.9%/3.5%，批尾 L5 缩短 19.0%/21.4%。\n\n【实测】Ling-3.0-Flash：BFCL 68.4→49.2 分钟（−28.1%）、SWE 166.9→149.5（−10.4%）、WideSearch 186.7→116.7（−37.5%）；Ling-3.1-Flash：SWE 234.1→185.1（−20.9%）、WideSearch 459.9→359.1（−21.9%）。SWE 消融最有说服力：同等并发下 Opt 保持 98.6%/98.3% 复用而 Baseline-2 仅 87.5%/80.4%，makespan 相对 Baseline-2 再降 24.4%/39.1%，新 prefill 降 88.9%/91.5%，TTFT 降 24.9%/50.2%、TPOT 降 51.1%/40.2%。MCP-Atlas：统一准入基线 466.1→Opt-FCFS 168.2 分钟（−63.9%）、333.5→140.5（−57.9%），再加 CAAS 分别再降 3.1% 与 8.5%（L5/L10 在 3.1 上降 29.1%/29.0%）。所有配置评测分数与基线对齐。

Conclusion: 本文的核心结论是：面向混合 LLM 的智能体批处理，效率瓶颈同时来自推理侧缓存/路由/调度与环境侧资源约束，必须协同优化。三个可迁移的原则：(a) 缓存比例与样本并发必须联合选取——单池耗尽引发的前缀重算会抵消并行收益，故应由工作负载画像推导平衡比与参考并发；(b) 轨迹标签是比 prompt 前缀匹配更廉价的复用识别信号，LBCH 在保持跨轮亲和的同时用负载边界抑制倾斜，RP 用"最近服务轨迹优先 + 选择性前缀查询"在缓存压力下低成本维持复用；(c) 解耦样本准入与环境执行可显著提升推理—环境重叠，CAAS 用已揭示的链深度推进长链以压缩批尾。局限与后续方向包括：容量模型为连续近似、忽略分配器粒度与碎片，比值需局部校准；RP 的标签集合与真实 GPU 缓存驻留可能不一致；CAAS 优先深链可能推迟浅链、且在宽松准入下优化配置的 L5 反而更长（因尾部任务构成不同，不宜单用 L5 跨准入策略比较）；未来可扩展到分层缓存、混合模型智能体场景的缓存淘汰策略，以及带 SLO（TTFT/TPOT）约束的 makespan 优化，并有望迁移到个人智能体服务与并行子智能体工作流。

Abstract: Efficient batch execution of agent tasks is critical to LLM training and development workflows, including benchmark evaluation, synthetic-data generation, and RL rollouts. Since these tasks alternate between LLM inference and environment interaction, we present coordinated optimizations to reduce batch makespan, the time required to complete all tasks in a batch. For hybrid LLMs, a workload-based resource model guides GPU-memory allocation between key-value (KV) cache and recurrent state and provides a reference sample concurrency to exploit parallelism while limiting recomputation. Trajectory-aware routing and scheduling promote cache reuse while balancing worker load. Under constrained environment capacity, we decouple sample admission from environment execution and introduce Chain-Advancing Action Scheduling (CAAS), which prioritizes long chains using observed progress to shorten the batch tail. Controlled replay combines actual inference with recorded environment responses and durations for ablations of individual optimizations. Live evaluations with Ling-3.0-Flash and Ling-3.1-Flash on the BFCL, SWE-bench Multilingual, WideSearch, and MCP-Atlas benchmarks demonstrate makespan reductions of 10.4% to 65.0%, while evaluation scores remain aligned. Furthermore, these methods have been successfully applied to training and evaluation workflows for the Ling-3.x model series, accelerating the model-development cycle.

</details>


### [379] [Reconstructing Fine-grained Memory Reuse Structure in GPU Kernels](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14741)
*Yanbo Zhao,Yueming Hao,Zecheng Li,Mao Lin,Shuyin Jiao,Keren Zhou,Xu Liu,Jiajia Li*

Main category: cs.DC

TL;DR: Optimizing GPU data movement requires knowing which instructions access the same data and across which execution scopes reuse occurs. Existing profilers can attribute memory behavior to individual instructions but do not expose the reuse relations among them, while aliasing, dynamic indexing, and runtime parameters prevent static analysis from establishing these relations in general. Cycle-level simulation can reconstruct such relations, but at costs prohibitive for production workloads. We introduce two abstractions for representing this structure: Topological Distance, which labels each dynamic memory access with the smallest execution scope (thread, warp, block, or grid) containing its most recent reuse, and PCDepGraph, which organizes these labels into a PC-level graph of the kernel's memory reuse structure. Defined over logical execution scopes rather than transient hardware state, the representation remains stable across runs and GPU targets while directly indicating the sharing scope that candidate optimization mechanisms must cover. Our tool, cuVein, reconstructs PCDepGraph directly from optimized binaries, without sampling, at generally under 10x overhead. Across HPC and AI workloads on NVIDIA RTX 4090 and H100, optimizations guided by PCDepGraph eliminate up to 90.18% of memory instructions and yield up to 2.84x kernel speedup; reuse-scope distributions remain consistent across platforms, supporting that the representation captures program structure rather than transient hardware behavior.

### [380] [SubGPU Pipelining: Intra-GPU Fine-Grained Spatial Parallelism for LLM Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14904)
*Muralidhar Andoorveedu,Marius Juston,Tingkai Liu,Sanjay Patel*

Main category: cs.DC

TL;DR: Large language model (LLM) decode is dominated by short, predominantly memory-bound kernels that make bursty use of on-chip execution resources and memory bandwidth. This paper introduces SubGPU Pipelining, a fine-grained, intra-GPU spatial execution model that cuts an operator graph into ordered contiguous segments, binds those segments to spatial stages backed by disjoint streaming-multiprocessor (SM) pools, and streams microbatches through the resulting schedule. Selecting the graph cuts, segment-to-stage binding, per-stage SM allocation, and microbatch size is a coupled optimization problem: each choice changes the overlap pattern, shared-resource contention, cache state, and execution times of the others. We evaluate SubGPU Pipelining through both simulation and silicon experiment using the GPT-OSS 120B workload with 32-GPU B200 deployment settings. The analytical shared-resource simulator searches across SubGPU pipeline structures and batch sizes to map the per-user/per-GPU throughput Pareto frontier. At matched per-GPU throughput, the modeled SubGPU frontier provides up to 2.2x higher per-user throughput than temporal execution, and at matched per-user throughput it provides up to 1.9x higher per-GPU throughput. To test physical feasibility and further validate the simulation results, silicon experiments are performed, using one B200 GPU to emulate a 32-GPU B200 deployment. The experiment evaluates one selected two-stage pipeline configuration at global batch 2,048 using CUDA Green Contexts and TensorRT-LLM kernels. Results show that SubGPU Pipelining improves mean DRAM read-plus-write throughput from 71.8% to 83.6% of peak, and reduces the 36-layer decoder iteration time by 10.33%.

Abstract: Large language model (LLM) decode is dominated by short, predominantly memory-bound kernels that make bursty use of on-chip execution resources and memory bandwidth. This paper introduces SubGPU Pipelining, a fine-grained, intra-GPU spatial execution model that cuts an operator graph into ordered contiguous segments, binds those segments to spatial stages backed by disjoint streaming-multiprocessor (SM) pools, and streams microbatches through the resulting schedule. Selecting the graph cuts, segment-to-stage binding, per-stage SM allocation, and microbatch size is a coupled optimization problem: each choice changes the overlap pattern, shared-resource contention, cache state, and execution times of the others. We evaluate SubGPU Pipelining through both simulation and silicon experiment using the GPT-OSS 120B workload with 32-GPU B200 deployment settings. The analytical shared-resource simulator searches across SubGPU pipeline structures and batch sizes to map the per-user/per-GPU throughput Pareto frontier. At matched per-GPU throughput, the modeled SubGPU frontier provides up to 2.2x higher per-user throughput than temporal execution, and at matched per-user throughput it provides up to 1.9x higher per-GPU throughput. To test physical feasibility and further validate the simulation results, silicon experiments are performed, using one B200 GPU to emulate a 32-GPU B200 deployment. The experiment evaluates one selected two-stage pipeline configuration at global batch 2,048 using CUDA Green Contexts and TensorRT-LLM kernels. Results show that SubGPU Pipelining improves mean DRAM read-plus-write throughput from 71.8% to 83.6% of peak, and reduces the 36-layer decoder iteration time by 10.33%.

</details>


### [381] [Recompute or Restore? Host-Tier KV for Multi-Model Agent Workflows on a Static-Graph NPU Serving Stack](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15126)
*Sungwon Woo,Seyeon Kim*

Main category: cs.DC

TL;DR: Agent workflows issue dependent model calls that share long context prefixes, so serving them efficiently depends on reusing the key-value (KV) cache of those prefixes. On accelerators that compile model graphs ahead of time, however, the device KV budget is fixed, and prefixes evicted under load must be recomputed. Restoring them from host memory avoids this recomputation, but the transfer occupies the same engine thread as prefill and decode, so its benefit is not guaranteed. In this paper, we study when restoring beats recomputing on a commercial static-graph neural processing unit (NPU) stack (Rebellions ATOM+, vllm-rbln 0.10.2) that serves a Qwen3-8B planner on two cards and a Qwen3-0.6B executor on one. We first show that repeated prefill dominates planner work when default serving collapses: 89.5% of the executed planner prompt tokens had been materialized before. We then build a synchronous host-DRAM tier on the runtime's public KV copy calls, together with a scheduler-aware event model whose predictions are frozen before each test cohort. Experimental results show that the host tier raises workflow service-level objective (SLO) attainment from 22.8% to 100% and from 9.4% to 99.8% in the two tested overload conditions, and endpoint confirmation on two new seeds supports conservative load gains of 11.8% (chain) and 18.2% (fork), while mixed and bursty workloads remain seed-sensitive. The frozen model predicts median and 99th-percentile (P99) latency within its 15% tolerance in all 24 common-load conditions, including the 16-18% P99 increase that the tier causes for fork workflows, but it misorders three policy contrasts and overestimates the benefit of a cheaper store path (11% predicted against 3.1% measured). The trade-off therefore depends on runtime scheduling and transfer cost as well as cache capacity.
